Details.OtherInformation: Probationary Periods: As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you may be required to serve a 1-year probationary period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider: your performance and conduct; the needs and interests of the agency; whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service. Upon completion of your probationary period your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest. Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP): This program applies to employees who have been involuntarily separated from a Federal service position within the competitive service or Federal service employees whose positions have been deemed surplus or no longer needed. To receive selection priority for this position, you must: (1) meet ICTAP eligibility criteria; (2) be rated well-qualified for the position with a score of 85 or above; and, (3) submit the appropriate documentation to support your ICTAP eligibility. Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended that would interfere with completing an online application, you may request an alternative application. Please send an email to the following address for information on how to obtain an alternative application: whs.job.application.assistance@mail.mil Reemployed Annuitants: Applicants in receipt of an annuity based on civilian employment in the Federal Service are subject to the DoD Policy on The Employment of Annuitants. /www.esd.whs.mil/DD/DoD-Issuances/140025/ Current or Former Political Appointees: Agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Nepotism: Under the provisions of 5 USC 3110, an individual may not be appointed into a position if the position is under the supervisory chain of command of a relative. Additional vacancies may be filled by this announcement.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-12, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service: Applying advanced statistical, economic, or operations-research principles to analyze and evaluate allowance-program issues and provide technical expertise on allowance programs. Leading complex analytical projects involving the development or substantial revision of data-collection approaches, analytical techniques, or program-evaluation criteria. Developing, presenting, and defending recommendations and analytical methodologies for complex allowance-program issues before senior officials, stakeholders, oversight bodies, or other public-facing audiences.; OR B. Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree. You may qualify at the GS-11, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service: Conducting comprehensive analyses of complex data using advanced statistical, economic, or data-science analytical and evaluative methods, and developing recommendations based on the results; Modifying or adapting standard data-science and statistical techniques to address a range of analytical challenges, program issues, or policy questions; Planning and carrying out complex studies, documenting and justifying findings, and presenting results to technical and nontechnical audiences, including senior officials. OR B. Master's or equivalent graduate degree. You may qualify at the GS-09, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service: Applying established statistical, economic, or data-science methods to analyze and evaluate data for routine projects or assignments; Independently using automated analytical tools, such as SQL, R, Python, or similar software, to extract, organize, and analyze information from complex data sources; Resolving conventional problems in data collection and analysis by applying established program methodologies, procedures, and regulations. OR B. 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree or master's or equivalent graduate degree. OR C. Possess some specialized experience as described, but less than one year; and have more than one year of graduate level education as described, but less than two. When added, the percentage of the requirements that you meet must total at least 100%. You may qualify at the GS-07, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-05 grade level in the Federal service: Assisting with developmental assignments by applying statistical, economic, or data-science principles, methods, and techniques under guidance; Using automated systems and software, such as SQL, R, Python, or similar tools, to access, retrieve, organize, and review data from multiple sources; Assisting with research, interpretation, and evaluation of data using qualitative and quantitative analytical techniques for well-precedented assignments. OR B. Possess: a Bachelor's degree w/Superior Academic Achievement or 1 year of graduate level education. OR C. Have some specialized experience as described, but less than one year; and I have some but less than one year of graduate level education as described. When added, the percentage of the requirements that you meet must total at least 100%. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 0110/1515/1530 series. If you are applying for the Economist 0110 series, you must have the following. Degree: economics, that included at least 21 semester hours in economics and 3 semester hours in statistics, accounting, or calculus. OR Combination of education and experience courses equivalent to a major in economics, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. If you are applying for the Operations Research 1515 series, you must have the following. Degree: in operations research; or at least 24 semester hours in a combination of operations research, mathematics, probability, statistics, mathematical logic, science, or subject-matter courses requiring substantial competence in college-level mathematics or statistics, Engineering (usually Industrial Engineering), Science, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, or Management Science, optimization; mathematical modeling; queueing theory; engineering; physics (except descriptive or survey courses); econometrics; psychometrics; biometrics; experimental psychology; physical chemistry; industrial process analysis; managerial economics; computer science; measurement for management; mathematical models in social phenomena; and courses that involved application of operations research techniques and methodologies to problems of management, marketing, systems design, and other specialized fields; or other comparable quantitative analysis courses. At least 3 of the 24 semester hours must have been in calculus. If you are applying for the Statistics 1530 series, you must have the following. Degree: that included 15 semester hours in statistics (or in mathematics and statistics, provided at least 6 semester hours were in statistics), and 9 additional semester hours in one or more of the following: physical or biological sciences, medicine, education, or engineering; or in the social sciences including demography, history, economics, social welfare, geography, international relations, social or cultural anthropology, health sociology, political science, public administration, psychology, etc. Credit toward meeting statistical course requirements should be given for courses in which 50 percent of the course content appears to be statistical methods, e.g., courses that included studies in research methods in psychology or economics such as tests and measurements or business cycles, or courses in methods of processing mass statistical data such as tabulating methods or electronic data processing. OR Combination of education and experience courses as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The experience should have included a full range of professional statistical work such as (a) sampling, (b) collecting, computing, and analyzing statistical data, and (c) applying statistical techniques such as measurement of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, sampling error, simple and multiple correlation, analysis of variance, and tests of significance.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Personnel Readiness Management Agency. The incumbent Serves in a developmental training interdisciplinary position as a Statistician (Economics),Economist, or Operations Research Analyst (Data Scientist) assisting in developing housing and cost-of-living allowances and providing support with managing certain aspects of the BAH, OHA, Overseas COLA, and CONUS COLA programs.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: DPAC is an operational component within PRMA and is designated to serve in direct analytic support to the military Services and OSD to conduct comprehensive analysis on how policy or environmental changes affect the performance or composition of the workforce. DPAC provides the go-to expertise for scientific assessments, data analytics, and outreach, to improve the lives of the DoD community.
MajorDuties: As a Interdisciplinary Statistician (Economics )/Economist/Operations Research Analyst (Data Scientist) at the GS-0110/1515/1530-7/9/11/12 some of your typical work assignments may include: GS-7 Serves in a developmental capacity, assisting senior analysts in developing housing and cost-of-living allowances (BAH, OHA, COLA). With close supervision, analyzes housing and cost-of-living data to help produce rate recommendations. Assists in researching economic issues and reviewing data reports and statistical summaries to support rate suggestions. Helps prepare reports, memorandums, and allowance materials for publication and dissemination. Assists the team in responding to inquiries regarding allowance programs and survey results. GS-9 Independently carries out recurring assignments to develop and analyze military housing and cost-of-living surveys. Analyzes statistical and economic data to produce allowance rate recommendations in conformance with accepted policies. Conducts in-depth reviews of data reports and statistical summaries, identifying and researching economic issues and facts for allowance determinations. Prepares recommendations, reports, and responses to customer inquiries on allowance programs with limited supervisory review. Designs and builds user-focused analytics to extract actionable information from diverse data sources to inform decision-makers. GS-11 Plans and conducts a variety of complex studies on housing and cost-of-living programs, resolving difficult issues and interpreting policy. Independently analyzes and defends rate-setting methodologies and makes recommendations that have a significant impact on service members. Develops and refines analytical methods and procedures for data collection, validation, and the accomplishment of surveys. Serves as a technical resource, providing professional assistance and advice to the Department on allowance programs. Prepares and presents detailed briefings, complex analyses, and justifications for multiple audiences to defend findings and program recommendations. GS-12 Serves as a senior analyst and subject matter expert responsible for the full lifecycle of developing, analyzing, and managing allowance programs. Leads the most complex and critical analyses of economic and statistical data, formulating and defending final rate recommendations for senior leadership approval. Presents and defends allowance programs and rate-setting methodologies against challenges and public scrutiny, representing the agency in high-level meetings. Develops and implements new analytical techniques and criteria to improve program effectiveness and advises management on long-range plans and objectives. Provides authoritative guidance and mentorship to junior analysts and coordinates with high-ranking officials across DoD, government agencies, and private sources.
Details.Education: ARE YOU USING YOUR EDUCATION TO QUALIFY or Satisfy the Individual Occupational Requirements? You MUST provide transcripts or other documentation to support your educational claims. Unofficial transcripts are acceptable at time of application. All materials must be submitted by the closing date of the announcement. GRADUATE EDUCATION: One academic year of graduate education is considered to be the number of credits hours that your graduate school has determined to represent one academic year of full-time study. Such study may have been performed on a full-time or part-time basis. If you cannot obtain your graduate school's definition of one year of graduate study, 18 semester hours (or 27 quarter hours) should be considered as satisfying the requirement for one year of full-time graduate study. FOREIGN EDUCATION may be qualifying if a private organization specializing in interpreting foreign education programs has deemed the foreign education equivalent to that gained in an accredited U.S. education program or a U.S. accredited college or university has given full credit for the foreign courses. Unofficial transcripts from U.S. Department of Education accredited colleges, universities, schools, or institutions listing your name, the name of the school, the date and degree awarded, and the list of classes and credits earned are acceptable for the application process. If selected, official transcripts are required before a firm job offer is made. A photocopy of your degree/diploma is not acceptable. When relying on foreign education, submit transcripts and a copy of the equivalency evaluation results letter with a course-by-course listing. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-12, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service: Applying advanced statistical, economic, or operations-research principles to analyze and evaluate allowance-program issues and provide technical expertise on allowance programs. Leading complex analytical projects involving the development or substantial revision of data-collection approaches, analytical techniques, or program-evaluation criteria. Developing, presenting, and defending recommendations and analytical methodologies for complex allowance-program issues before senior officials, stakeholders, oversight bodies, or other public-facing audiences. OR B. Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree. You may qualify at the GS-11, if you fulfill the following qualifications: B. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service: Conducting comprehensive analyses of complex data using advanced statistical, economic, or data-science analytical and evaluative methods, and developing recommendations based on the results. Modifying or adapting standard data-science and statistical techniques to address a range of analytical challenges, program issues, or policy questions. Planning and carrying out complex studies, documenting and justifying findings, and presenting results to technical and nontechnical audiences, including senior officials. OR B. Master's or equivalent graduate degree. You may qualify at the GS-09, if you fulfill the following qualifications: C. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service: Applying established statistical, economic, or data-science methods to analyze and evaluate data for routine projects or assignments. Independently using automated analytical tools, such as SQL, R, Python, or similar software, to extract, organize, and analyze information from complex data sources. Resolving conventional problems in data collection and analysis by applying established program methodologies, procedures, and regulations. OR B. 2 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a master's degree or master's or equivalent graduate degree. OR C. Possess some specialized experience as described, but less than one year; and have more than one year of graduate level education as described, but less than two. When added, the percentage of the requirements that you meet must total at least 100%. You may qualify at the GS-07, if you fulfill the following qualifications: D. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-05 grade level in the Federal service: Assisting with developmental assignments by applying statistical, economic, or data-science principles, methods, and techniques under guidance. Using automated systems and software, such as SQL, R, Python, or similar tools, to access, retrieve, organize, and review data from multiple sources. Assisting with research, interpretation, and evaluation of data using qualitative and quantitative analytical techniques for well-precedented assignments. OR B. Possess: a Bachelor's degree w/Superior Academic Achievement or 1 year of graduate level education. OR C. Have some specialized experience as described, but less than one year; and I have some but less than one year of graduate level education as described. When added, the percentage of the requirements that you meet must total at least 100%. In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 0110/1515/1530 series. E. If you are applying for the Economist 0110 series, you must have the following. Degree: economics, that included at least 21 semester hours in economics and 3 semester hours in statistics, accounting, or calculus. OR Combination of education and experience courses equivalent to a major in economics, as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. F. If you are applying for the Operations Research 1515 series, you must have the following. Degree: in operations research; or at least 24 semester hours in a combination of operations research, mathematics, probability, statistics, mathematical logic, science, or subject-matter courses requiring substantial competence in college-level mathematics or statistics, Engineering (usually Industrial Engineering), Science, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, or Management Science, optimization; mathematical modeling; queueing theory; engineering; physics (except descriptive or survey courses); econometrics; psychometrics; biometrics; experimental psychology; physical chemistry; industrial process analysis; managerial economics; computer science; measurement for management; mathematical models in social phenomena; and courses that involved application of operations research techniques and methodologies to problems of management, marketing, systems design, and other specialized fields; or other comparable quantitative analysis courses. At least 3 of the 24 semester hours must have been in calculus. G. If you are applying for the Statistics 1530 series, you must have the following. Degree: that included 15 semester hours in statistics (or in mathematics and statistics, provided at least 6 semester hours were in statistics), and 9 additional semester hours in one or more of the following: physical or biological sciences, medicine, education, or engineering; or in the social sciences including demography, history, economics, social welfare, geography, international relations, social or cultural anthropology, health sociology, political science, public administration, psychology, etc. Credit toward meeting statistical course requirements should be given for courses in which 50 percent of the course content appears to be statistical methods, e.g., courses that included studies in research methods in psychology or economics such as tests and measurements or business cycles, or courses in methods of processing mass statistical data such as tabulating methods or electronic data processing. OR Combination of education and experience courses as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The experience should have included a full range of professional statistical work such as (a) sampling, (b) collecting, computing, and analyzing statistical data, and (c) applying statistical techniques such as measurement of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, sampling error, simple and multiple correlation, analysis of variance, and tests of significance. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. *NOTE: Failure to provide transcripts will result in you being rated ineligible for this position.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Human Resources Activity (Personnel Readiness Management Agency) . The incumbent Serves in a developmental training interdisciplinary position as a Statistician (Economics),Economist, or Operations Research Analyst (Data Scientist) assisting in developing housing and cost-of-living allowances and providing support with managing certain aspects of the BAH, OHA, Overseas COLA, and CONUS COLA programs.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: DPAC is an operational component within DHRA (PRMA) and is designated to serve in direct analytic support to the military Services and OSD to conduct comprehensive analysis on how policy or environmental changes affect the performance or composition of the workforce. DPAC provides the go-to expertise for scientific assessments, data analytics, and outreach, to improve the lives of the DoD community.
MajorDuties: As a Interdisciplinary Statistician (Economics )/Economist/Operations Research Analyst (Data Scientist) at the GS-0110/1515/1530-7/9/11/12 some of your typical work assignments may include: GS-7 Serves in a developmental capacity, assisting senior analysts in developing housing and cost-of-living allowances (BAH, OHA, COLA). With close supervision, analyzes housing and cost-of-living data to help produce rate recommendations. Assists in researching economic issues and reviewing data reports and statistical summaries to support rate suggestions. Helps prepare reports, memorandums, and allowance materials for publication and dissemination. Assists the team in responding to inquiries regarding allowance programs and survey results. GS-9 Independently carries out recurring assignments to develop and analyze military housing and cost-of-living surveys. Analyzes statistical and economic data to produce allowance rate recommendations in conformance with accepted policies. Conducts in-depth reviews of data reports and statistical summaries, identifying and researching economic issues and facts for allowance determinations. Prepares recommendations, reports, and responses to customer inquiries on allowance programs with limited supervisory review. Designs and builds user-focused analytics to extract actionable information from diverse data sources to inform decision-makers. GS-11 Plans and conducts a variety of complex studies on housing and cost-of-living programs, resolving difficult issues and interpreting policy. Independently analyzes and defends rate-setting methodologies and makes recommendations that have a significant impact on service members. Develops and refines analytical methods and procedures for data collection, validation, and the accomplishment of surveys. Serves as a technical resource, providing professional assistance and advice to the Department on allowance programs. Prepares and presents detailed briefings, complex analyses, and justifications for multiple audiences to defend findings and program recommendations. GS-12 Serves as a senior analyst and subject matter expert responsible for the full lifecycle of developing, analyzing, and managing allowance programs. Leads the most complex and critical analyses of economic and statistical data, formulating and defending final rate recommendations for senior leadership approval. Presents and defends allowance programs and rate-setting methodologies against challenges and public scrutiny, representing the agency in high-level meetings. Develops and implements new analytical techniques and criteria to improve program effectiveness and advises management on long-range plans and objectives. Provides authoritative guidance and mentorship to junior analysts and coordinates with high-ranking officials across DoD, government agencies, and private sources.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. Have one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal Service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) which has given me the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties related to the position being filled. Specialized experience is defined as: Overseeing or conducting data-driven industrial base analyses integrating supply chain risk management, economic, and acquisition/budgetary data to assess vulnerabilities and inform policy or investment decisions; leading or participating on cross-functional teams (including interagency, industry, or defense stakeholders) to identify and prioritize supply chain risks; and preparing strategic documentation, policy recommendations, or briefing materials for senior leadership regarding industrial capability, defense authorities (such as the Defense Production Act or related industrial base investment mechanisms), or program investments. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. Your resume may not exceed two (2) pages. For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the duration of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume at https://help.usajobs.gov/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, as part of their application package, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, indicating the service member is otherwise eligible and will be discharged or released within 120 days from the date of submission.. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. This "certification" must include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable), and date any terminal leave will begin. It must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible". Members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if they are on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level. Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Department of War Office of the Inspector General (DoW OIG), Office of Legislative Affairs and Communications (OLAC) and reports to the Legislative and Public Affairs Director. This position supervises and leads congressional affairs activities for DoW OIG, developing outreach strategies, coordinating responses to Congress, monitoring legislation, maintaining congressional relationships, and preparing leadership for hearings.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of Legislative Affairs and Communications
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Engaged Oversight Professionals Dedicated to Improving the Department of War Come join us for a meaningful career with an agency that truly values its employees. We detect and deter fraud, waste, and abuse in DoW programs and operations; promote the economy, efficiency, and effectiveness of the DoW; and help ensure ethical conduct throughout the DoW. For more information about who we are and what we're about, please visit www.dodig.mil.
MajorDuties: Formulates and executes strategic outreach plans to engage Congress and communicate DoW OIG programs, priorities, and authorities.
Synthesizes information across DoW OIG components and leads coordination of timely, accurate responses to congressional inquiries.
Develops strategies and maintains strong working relationships with congressional staff; conducts proactive and responsive engagements.
Monitors legislative actions, analyzes impacts on DoW OIG operations, and develops strategies for responding to legislative changes.
Prepares DoW OIG leaders for hearings, manages testimony development, background materials, advance Q and A, and post-hearing submissions.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-09, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service: Performing recurring administrative duties, coordinating office support functions, and maintaining organized tracking systems or databases to ensure efficient daily program operations; Gathering, compiling, and consolidating data or reports from established sources to assist higher-level analysts in evaluating program efficiency or compliance; Serving as an initial point of contact for office inquiries, distributing information to staff, and assisting in the preparation of routine correspondence or standardized meeting materials. OR; B. I have master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B. or J.D., if related; OR; C. You have some specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and you have more than one year but less than two years of education as described in B. You have computed the percentage of the requirements that you meet, and the total is at least 100%. (To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then divide your semester hours of graduate education beyond the first year by 18. Add the two percentages. The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.) You may qualify at the GS-11, if you fulfill the following qualifications: A. One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service: Analyzing administrative processes and operational data to recommend strategic adjustments to internal workflows, guidelines, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that enhance office efficiency. Monitoring and coordinating administrative program areas (such as procurement tracking, records disposition, or contract deliverables) to ensure strict compliance with federal and agency regulations. Collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders to resolve moderately complex administrative issues, advising staff on regulatory applications, and drafting non-routine reports or briefings on program status. OR; B. I possess 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education or Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree (such as LL.M.). OR; C. You have some specialized experience as described in A, but less than one year; and you have more than one year but less than two years of education as described in B. You have computed the percentage of the requirements that you meet, and the total is at least 100%. (To compute the percentage, divide your total months of qualifying experience by 12. Then divide your semester hours of graduate education beyond the first year by 18. Add the two percentages. The total percentage must equal at least 100 percent to qualify.) Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. *NOTE: Failure to provide transcripts will result in you being rated ineligible for this position.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Human Resources Activity. The incumbent will serve as a Program Support Specialist for DPAC responsible for executing administrative policies and procedures.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The DPAC mission is to improve the readiness, well-being, and security of the Total Force by conducting evidence-based research, personnel analytics, and market communications efforts.
MajorDuties: As a Program Support Specialist at the GS-0301-9/11 some of your typical work assignments may include: GS-09: Duties Performs daily administrative and program support tasks, including organizing digital files and program records in accordance with established agency guidelines. Tracks operational and personnel data in standardized databases or tracking sheets, identifying and flagging missing information for higher-level review. Serves as a customer service and information liaison for the office, answering routine inquiries, assisting visitors, and routing incoming administrative and operational requests to the appropriate staff members. Coordinates initial onboarding logistics for incoming personnel, to include account requests and logistical access. Reviews basic contract documents, monthly invoices, and Government Purchase Card (GPC) transactions for accuracy, highlighting discrepancies for higher-level review. GS-11: Duties Serves as a Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) or alternate COR, independently monitoring contractor performance against the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP), reviewing deliverables, and certifying invoices. Supports the records management program by conducting routine audits, maintaining file plans, and adhering to proper lifecycle disposition procedures. Coordinates multi-divisional data calls by designing standardized response templates, tracking submissions, and consolidating quantitative and qualitative data for senior leadership review. Reviews and processes various administrative and operational requests, ensuring strict compliance with regulations and internal DoW financial guidelines. Provides independent administrative and operational support for assigned programs, managing project milestones, tracking administrative actions, and presenting regular status updates to leadership.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Defense Human Resources Activity. The incumbent will be responsible for providing overall support functions to the entire DTMO. Those support functions include developing DTMO's strategic direction; developing and monitoring performance metrics for travel programs and initiatives; facilitating support agreements on behalf of DTMO's many customers; overseeing acquisition processes to ensure DTMO obtains support services.
MajorDuties: This position is being filled under the memorandum from the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness (USD(P&R)) "Expansion of Direct Hire Authority for Certain Personnel of the Department of Defense," dated October 15, 2021. As a Supervisory Program Analyst (Operations Support) at the GS-0343-14 some of your typical work assignments may include: Serves as Supervisory Program Analyst/Business Operations Branch, providing overall direction for organizational strategic planning, performance management and travel data analysis. Designs and implements organization's strategic planning program, providing technical expertise and knowledge to implement strategic planning processes, policies, and initiatives, and monitors and tracks progress. Tracks progress and assesses performance of travel programs and key initiatives, overseeing the development of measures and supporting dashboards that provide credible, decision ready business intelligence to support management decisions, reporting, compliance, resource allocation, and risk management. Directs and oversees analytical studies using DoD Travel Enterprise data to better understand travel spend, develop program recommendations, and travel policy formulation, and identify cost savings/efficiencies. Oversees DTMO's Financial Improvement and Audit Remediation (FIAR) and Managers' Internal Control Program (MICP); assesses internal controls and makes recommendations for improvements, designs and implements test of controls for key functional areas, prepares evaluation documentation, and works to limit organization's overall risk. Provides oversight for Contract Officer's Representative and Support Agreement Manager duties ensuring that all contracts, internal and externally are funded, awarded on time and services are received.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-13, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes: (1) Working with f Air Force, Joint Staff, Department of Defense, Functional Area Management (FAM) requirements, methods, practices, procedures, regulations, policies, laws, and processes to formulate, justify and execute functions, processes and various logistical aspects in support of the mission, structure, goals, work processes and programs; (2) Working with coordinating and negotiating funding/resource and planning issues with Service, DoD, and other agencies; and (3) Working with all aspects of Strategic Management, including environmental assessments (internal & external to the organization), formulation of strategy (through visioning, goals & objectives determination, organizational mission realities, core competencies, and synchronized functional internal business processes), implementation of strategy (understanding leadership and organizational learning aspects), and lastly the evaluation of strategy (strategic control). FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-13 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-14 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of Air Force, Joint Staff, Department of Defense, Functional Area Management (FAM) requirements methods, practices, procedures, regulations, policies, laws, and processes to formulate, justify, and execute, functions, processes and various logistical functions and support of the mission, structure, goals, work processes, and programs of assigned organizations. Knowledge of missions, programs, roles, functions, goals, objectives, work processes, organizational structures, sources of funding, resources, and operation of the DoD, Air Force, and organizations that govern, interface with, and/or influence the PPBS (budget and the planning and programming process) to ensure effective medical service deliberate and crisis action planning, operations, and execution. Knowledge of the organizational structure, policies, procedures, plans, regulations, and laws of the ANG, NGB, AF/Service components, Congress, and DoD that effect funding and program requirements. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, procedures, and ability to apply laws, executive orders, regulations, policies, and concepts pertaining to strategy, doctrine, and medical response programs. Skill to analyze, plan, organize, recommend changes, develop alternatives, and direct the functions and staff in critical aspects of the Joint Operational Plans and Execution system and to facilitate PPBS budgetary/resource procurement and planning and programming to meet program requirements and objectives within available resources or develop recommendations for budgetary or planning actions under conditions of time pressure and uncertainty due to: short and rapidly changing program and budgetary deadlines and objectives; gaps and conflicts in program and budgetary information; lack of predictive data; conflicting program and budgetary objectives; and changing guidelines for the work. Ability to gain cooperation from others through tact, courtesy, diplomacy with special emphasis on communication ability to both orally and in writing justify, defend, present, and/or advise on processes/actions. Ability to motivate, mentor, appraise, and work with supervisors and non-supervisory employees. Ability to coordinate and negotiate funding/resource and planning issues with ANG/AF/Service, DoD, and other agencies. Knowledge of all aspects of Strategic Management, including environmental assessments (internal & external to the organization), formulation of strategy (through visioning, goals & objectives determination, organizational mission realities, core competencies, and synchronized functional internal business processes), implementation of strategy (understanding leadership and organizational learning aspects), and lastly the evaluation of strategy (strategic control). Knowledge of personnel management principles as they relate to supervisory duties. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: Click on "Learn more about this agency" button below to view Eligibilities being considered and other IMPORTANT information. The primary purpose of this position is: Serve as a Program Manager responsible for performing the full range of medical readiness plans and operations in addition to the role of primary Manpower Functional Area Manager. The position will analyze tasks relative to ANG medical plans, operations, manpower, and analytics.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win...Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. Click here to view the AF Civilian Employment Eligibility Guide: 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans AF DCIPS Interchange AF Internal Employee DoD Transfer (Excluding Air Force) EO 12721 Certain Former Overseas Employees EO 13473 Appointment of Certain Military Spouses Former Federal Employees (Reinstatement) Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Employee Military Spouse Preference National Service (Peace Corps and VISTA) Non-AF DCIPS Interchange Non-Appropriated Fund Non-DoD Transfer Other (Interchange Agreements) People with Disabilities, Schedule A PPP DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technicians PPP DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible PPP Mil Res (MR) and Nat Guard (NG) Pref Eligible Technician Receiving Disability Retirement Special Inspector General for Afghanistan Reconstruction Veterans Employment Opportunities Act
MajorDuties: Plans, organizes, and directs the activities of the Medical Plans and Operations Branch; ensuring that work complies with legal and regulatory requirements and meets customer needs. Represents the Branch and/or Division with a variety of functional area organizations. Establishes, develops, and maintains effective working relationships with field personnel, other ANGRC Directorates, NGB, AF, AFRC, other service components, DoD, SECDEF, MAJCOMs, Congress, Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs, and contractors. Performs ongoing evaluation and analysis of ANG Medical Service manpower, analytics and plans in support of major Air National Guard missions and operational plans. Analyzes the effect of updates in plans on manpower and readiness reporting; identifying changes in areas where necessary. Actively participates in strategic planning to improve organizational direction and focus using strategic planning tools and techniques. Performs supervisory personnel management responsibilities.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. GS-11 SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-09, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes working knowledge and skill in applying CPI analytical and evaluative methods and techniques to issues or studies concerning the efficiency and effectiveness of program operations carried out by administrative or professional personnel, or substantive administrative support organizations. Working knowledge of pertinent laws, regulations, instructions, policies, and precedents which affect the use of program and related support resources in the area studied. OR EDUCATION: Successfully completed a Ph.D or equivalent graduate degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of the position. NOTE: You must submit copies of your college transcripts. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: I have a combination of specialized experience and education. A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts. GS-12 SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-11, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes skill in adapting analytical techniques and evaluation criteria to the measurement and improvement of program effectiveness and/or organizational productivity. Skill in developing new or modified work methods, organizational structures, management processes, and/or program administration procedures. Working knowledge of the major issues, program goals and objectives, work processes and administrative operations of the organization. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. One year at the GS-09 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-11 level. One year at the GS-11 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-12 level. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of Department of Defense (DoD), Joint Service and Air Force management engineering, organization and CPI principles, concepts, and methodologies. 2. Knowledge of process improvement techniques such as Lean Six Sigma, benchmarking, metric/statistical analysis, and process flow charting. 3. Skill in applying analytical and evaluative methods and techniques used to resolve complex problems of a broad range of functional areas related to CPI. 4. Ability and skill using PC to operate data base management systems, requirements analysis, and data manipulation and extraction techniques. 5. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing; skill in conducting interviews with employees, supervisors, and management officials at MAJCOM and HQ USAF to obtain information about organizational missions, functions, and work procedures. 6. Ability to carry out and complete assignments involving complex work with diverse and dynamic groups by gaining their cooperation with tact, courtesy, and diplomacy and moving them towards an ownership of their objective without imposing personal bias. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT: This is a developmental position that leads to the full performance level. The incumbent will receive on-the-job training designed to provide the opportunity to perform the duties at the full performance level. The incumbent may be noncompetitively promoted to the next performance level upon (1) satisfactorily completing the training requirements (2) satisfactorily performing at the next performance level (3) meeting all OPM legal and regulatory requirements for promotion and (4) recommendation for promotion by the supervisor.

MajorDuties: GS-11/12 Studies the structure and/or functions of organizations with interrelated work processes and functions and accurately advises or proposes solutions to improvement processes and maximize mission accomplishment and resources utilization. Resolves complicated substantive problems affecting programs and requirements, and proposes new process flows, organizational structures, realignment of functions, and/or staffing levels to improve efficiency. Designs, plans, and conducts work measurement, methods and procedures, manpower requirements utilization and engineered time standards; reviews and implements changes to organization and resource controls/programs, and/or benchmarking studies of complex, interrelated substantive work processes or functions. Studies require significant adaptation of work methods and application of manpower/process standards. Designs, plans, and facilitates CPI events, manpower assessments, management surveys, and research projects, providing advisory services of a wide variety on substantive issues with extensive scope, complexity, and impact, assessing the overall effectiveness of program operations. Lead facilitator in review and studies to determine the most efficient and cost-effective means of accomplishment. Provides complex management support services in the areas of strategic planning alignment, program manpower cost analysis, annual/multi-year/long range fiscal planning (e.g., Defense Planning Guidance (DPG), Planning, Programming, and Budgeting System (PPBS) cycles), and development of annual work plan(s), and/or commercial activity for organization(s) whose operations are interrelated and unstable. Actively participates and facilitates management studies and strategic planning to improve organizational direction and focus using appropriate strategic planning tools and techniques.

Designing and conducting comprehensive studies, and preparing solutions to especially broad, important, and severe operational and contingency exercise planning scenarios. Knowledge of the various ANG flying communities and their Major Design Series (MDS) weapons systems. The skill to work in a flying community and inter-agency environment with a strong knowledge of ANG organizations, processes, and procedures. MajorDuties: The primary purpose of this position: NGB/A3, Air, Space, and Information Operations Directorate develops and implements policy to Organize, Train, Equip and Deploy Air National Guard (ANG) Combat Ready Forces in Support of State, Combatant Command, and Services Requirements Worldwide. 1.Manages senior ANG aviation exercise Action Officers (AO) who collect, review and determine worldwide exercise requirements for ANG participation, attends exercise planning conferences, and organizes ANG aviation support to, and participation in, selected exercises. 2.Provides subject matter expertise and guidance on exercise processes and procedures to ensure selected exercises meet and support ANG aviation training, combat readiness, and Building Partnership Capacity BPC objectives. 3.Serves as the ANG established aviation exercise point of contact with States, Coalition Partners, Joint & Service staffs, NAFs, wings, foreign nationals & civic leaders on Combatant Command (COCOM), National Exercise Program (NEP), DoD Chairman's Exercise Program (CEP), Joint Exercise Program (JEP) and Service Exercises. 4.Functions as the Office Conducting Exercise (OCE) in the management planning, and facilitation of internal ANG exercises as well as staff members assigned to direct ANG exercise actions and chairs the ANG Aviation Exercise Participation Working Group. 5.Performs first level supervisory personnel management responsibilities.

Online Application: Questionnaire Resume: Your resume may NOT exceed two pages, and the font size should not be smaller than 10 pts. You will not be considered for this vacancy if your resume is illegible/unreadable. Additional information on resume requirements can be located under "How To Apply". Transcripts/Registration/License: If qualifying on education/position requires education, you must submit copies of your transcripts and if required for the position, submit an active, current registration/license. Veterans: If claiming VEOA, VRA or 30% Disabled Veteran - Submit VOW certification memo or copy of the official DD Form 214, which must include the character of service (i.e., with an honorable or general discharge). This will be annotated in block 24 on member copy 2, 4, or 7 of the DD Form 214. If claiming 30% Disabled Veteran, you must also submit a VA Letter or a disability determination from a branch of the Armed Forces. NOTE: All veterans claiming 10-point preference must also submit a SF-15 form. Current or Former Federal Civilian Employees (includes current Air Force employees): You must submit a legible copy of your most recent SF-50, Notification of Personnel Action, AND a SF-50 reflecting the highest grade held if different from your recent SF-50. The SF-50, block 24 must contain "1" or "2" AND block 34 must be a "1". Employees eligible under an OPM approved interchange agreement, block 34 may contain a "1" or "2". Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. The certification memo must originate from the member's military service branch on official letterhead and contain the following: Name/Rank/Grade of Service Member Branch of Armed Forces Dates of Active Service (Start and End Date(s) Expected Date of Discharge/Release from Active Duty Terminal leave start date (if applicable) Expected character of service (honorable or general) and type of separation (i.e. separation or retirement) Must be certified within 120 days of anticipated discharge Signature by, or by direction of the adjutant, personnel office, unit commander, or higher headquarters commander. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form 214 must be submitted upon receipt. OPTIONAL DOCUMENTS: Performance Appraisals for Current Federal Civilian Employees - Most recent performance appraisals (dated within last 3 years) showing the official rating of record, signed by a supervisor, or statement why the performance appraisal is unavailable. Awards for Current Federal Civilian employees - List any awards received within the last 3 years on the resume. Note: Applicant must not submit award Notification of Personnel Actions (SF50s).

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-14, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes: (1) Working with Title 10 USC 1554a, Review of Separation Disability, and DoDI 6040.44, Lead Component for the Physical Disability Board of Review; (2) Working with a wide range of concepts, principles, and practices relating to program management, budget execution, civilian personnel matters, and manpower and organization issues and (3) Working with Air Force programs, goals and objectives, the sequence and timing of key operational events and milestones, methods of evaluating the effectiveness of planning actions as related to Physical Disability Review Board (PDBR) events. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-14 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-15 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of Title 10 USC 1554a, Review of Separation Disability, and DoDI 6040.44, Lead Component for the Physical Disability Board of Review. Knowledge of a wide range of concepts, principles, and practices relating to program management, budget execution, civilian personnel matters, and manpower and organization issues. Knowledge of Air Force programs, goals and objectives, the sequence and timing of key operational events and milestones, methods of evaluating the effectiveness of planning actions as related to PDBR events. Knowledge of USAF, DoD, and Federal programs, practices, guidelines, policies, regulations and laws related to all aspects of resource and program management. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the resource management functions, along with the ability to mentor and guide a staff on resource management matters. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MajorDuties: Plans, organizes, and directs the activities of the Medical Support Directorate, ensuring that medical evidence, clinical records, and physical standards complies with legal and regulatory requirements and meets customer needs. Exercises supervisory personnel management responsibilities. Advises and provides counsel to employees regarding policies, procedures, and directives of management Serves as the President, DoD Physical Disability Board of Review (PDBR), as determined by the Director, Air Force Review Boards Agency (AFBRA) and the Secretary of the Air Force, under delegated authority by the Department of Defense. Functions as the principal advisor over the DoD Physical Disability Board of Review operation as determined by the Director, Air Force Review Boards Agency. Provides strategic oversight of the staff that addresses a full range of medical issues and concerns raised by the applicant on medical issues and the interpretation of laws, medical standards, and policies defining a physical disability and the application by the PDBR. Represents the PDBR and AFBRA in all matters related to assigned and functional project areas.
