MajorDuties: The United States Space Force (USSF) at the Pentagon is searching for a Deputy Director of Staff to support HQSF/S347 (NH-0343-04, GS 14/15 equivalent). Description: The Office of the Deputy Chief of Space Operations for Operations is seeking an accomplished Deputy Director of Staff to help lead the integration, planning, and execution of a high-tempo headquarters organization. This is a senior, non-supervisory opportunity for a professional who can independently organize complex work, shape strategic outcomes, and turn broad leadership priorities into coordinated actions, clear decisions, and measurable results. As the Deputy Director of Staff, you will work directly with senior military and civilian leaders to integrate competing priorities, lead complex staff actions, resolve cross-functional challenges, and sustain momentum on high-visibility initiatives. You will develop strategic plans, executive correspondence, decision-quality briefings, policies, and recommendations that improve organizational effectiveness and enable mission success. The successful candidate is a trusted advisor, relationship builder, and collaborative problem-solver who performs well amid ambiguity and compressed timelines. You will thrive in this role if you bring mature judgment, strong accountability, exceptional communication skills, and the ability to influence outcomes while remaining aligned with leadership intent and the needs of the broader team. Ideal Candidate: The ideal candidate is an exceptionally capable, accountable, and collaborative senior professional who can independently lead complex, high-visibility staff actions in a fast-paced headquarters environment. The candidate will bring sound judgment, initiative, strategic perspective, and the ability to translate broad leadership intent into coordinated action, practical solutions, and decision-quality products. The candidate must demonstrate success operating in ambiguity; managing multiple competing priorities; and leading through influence, expertise, and relationships rather than formal authority. They will be an effective integrator and negotiator who builds trust across organizational boundaries, gains consensus among stakeholders with differing interests, and strengthens the performance of the broader team. The ideal candidate will possess: - Demonstrated experience independently leading complex initiatives at Service Headquarters, Combatant Command, Joint Staff, or OSW-levels - Exceptional personal accountability and follow-through; proactively identifies issues, develops options, manages risk, and drives actions to completion. - Ability to influence, integrate, negotiate, and build consensus among senior leaders, action officers, mission partners, and external stakeholders. - Exercises independent judgment and drives outcomes decisively, while remaining aligned with leadership intent, responsive to evolving priorities, and constructive in incorporating diverse perspectives. - Excellent relationship-building skills and a collaborative leadership style that earns trust, facilitates teamwork, and enables mission outcomes. - Ability to take broad or ambiguous direction and turn it into executable plans, milestones, coordinated taskings, governance processes, and decision products. - Experience in strategic planning, organizational effectiveness, policy development, workforce and workload analysis, resource prioritization, and senior-leader support. - Superior oral and written communication skills, including preparation of executive correspondence, briefings, decision memoranda, position papers, staff packages, reports, and recommendations. - Experience representing an organization in senior-level forums and communicating effectively with military, civilian, joint, interagency, and other mission partners. - Ability to mentor, guide, and elevate the work of others through technical expertise, thoughtful feedback, and professional example.

Promotion is not guaranteed, and no promise of promotion is implied. In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. You may qualify at the GS-09 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability to Assist with daily office administrative duties, including monitoring office supply inventories, placing standard orders, submitting routine IT or equipment maintenance requests, and greeting or routing visitors; Entering, updating, and maintaining tracking information in electronic databases or spreadsheets; AND Coordinating routine meeting rooms, adjusting simple calendar invites. OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Criminal justice, Security Management, or Law Enforcement and Administration. OR Combination of Education and Experience You may qualify at the GS-11 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability to Coordinate calendars and meeting requests for program managers or department directors; Reviewing incoming mail or electronic tasks to route them to the correct staff member; AND Tracking the status of active assignments and deadlines across a team to ensure on-time completion. OR Education: Ph.D or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Criminal justice, Security Management, or Law Enforcement and Administration. OR Combination of education and experience. You may qualify at the GS-12 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability to Manage the daily calendars, meeting requests, and complex scheduling for executives, senior directors, or board-level leaders; Reviewing and controlling incoming correspondence and action items to identify appropriate department owners and deadlines; AND Conducting quick-turn research, administrative studies, and assessments of office workflows to improve operational efficiency or address emergency situations. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Washington Headquarters Services (WHS) is a world-class service organization, with a dynamic workforce and unwavering commitment to service excellence. WHS is the essential services provider for the Office of the Secretary of War (OSW), Department of War (DoW) agencies, and offices in the National Capital Region.
MajorDuties: Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Directs comprehensive administrative and logistical operations for the WHS SESD Director and Deputy Director, including time and attendance reporting, procurement of office supplies, IT coordination, and protocol support for special ceremonies and VIP functions. Evaluates and processes complex, sensitive administrative projects, studies, and requests; drafts original correspondence for executive signature and synthesizes divergent inputs from federal and private-sector entities into unified briefs. Designs and compiles detailed read-ahead packages and reference portfolios for Director-level decision meetings, summarizing lengthy technical reports and verifying key facts to facilitate rapid, executive-level decision-making. Manages the master calendars for the Director and Deputy Director, forecasting recurring events, resolving scheduling conflicts, and serving as the primary liaison for Senior Executive Service (SES) principals, action officers, and joint stakeholders. Conducts high-priority, quick-turn studies and assessments on unique organizational issues, partnering with OSW, OJCS, and Military Departments to retrieve data, analyze findings, and recommend policy solutions for emergency or un-precedented situations.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility will be based upon a clear showing the applicant has education, training, and experience of the scope and quality sufficient to effectively carry-out the duties of the position. Candidates must exemplify the corporate perspective, leadership vision, broad experience and character needed in the SES corps not only to satisfy the immediate vacancy, but future vacancies which will occur in a variety of organizations, functions and locations. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. In accordance with new OPM requirements to streamline Senior Executive Service (SES) hiring, applicants are no longer required to submit lengthy narrative essays, including those for Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or Mandatory Technical Qualifications (TQs), when applying. Instead, the initial application will be resume-only, capped at two pages. This change streamlines the application process and more closely aligns with private industry practices. Applicants identified for potential selection will have their ECQs assessed by undergoing a structured interview with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Review Board (QRB). To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the education, Technical Qualifications (TQ), and Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) related to this position within your resume (not to exceed 2 pages). Resumes over the 2-page limit will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. CERTIFICATIONS: Level III APDP Program Management TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that satisfy the technical qualifications. TQ1: Demonstrated expertise in leading enterprise-level PPBE execution, overseeing multi-billion-dollar RDT&E and procurement portfolios, and ensuring resources are aligned to support rapid capability delivery. Proven ability to direct cost, schedule, and performance reporting for senior leadership and to manage Special Access Program governance across diverse mission areas. Extensive experience developing, codifying, and implementing acquisition policies and procedures and managing enterprise acquisition review forums that enable timely decisions for development, production, and fielding. TQ2: Exceptional capability in leading enterprise integration, acquisition policy development, and stakeholder alignment across headquarters, field commands, and interagency partners. Demonstrated success in building and directing cross-functional teams responsible for policy development, PPBE execution, SAP oversight, and strategic integration. Recognized for fostering collaborative relationships, ensuring stakeholder perspectives are accurately represented in senior decision forums, and shaping organizational structures and workforce competencies that strengthen long-term space acquisition integration. TQ3: Superior qualifications in providing senior advisory support on acquisition programs, legislative matters, and enterprise strategy. Extensive experience preparing senior officials for Congressional testimony, developing responses to Congressional inquiries, and maintaining effective relationships with Members of Congress and staff. Proven ability to represent senior leadership in engagements with OSW, military departments, industry, GAO, foreign partners, and other stakeholders. Demonstrated skill in developing SAP legislative strategies, resolving complex policy issues, and supporting crisis planning and exercises outside normal duty hours. TQ4: Advanced proficiency in leading large, technically complex acquisition organizations and shaping enterprise strategy, workforce development, and organizational performance. Holds Level III APDP Program Management certification and possesses extensive experience managing major defense acquisition programs, including international and multi-agency efforts. Demonstrated ability to develop acquisition talent pipelines, strengthen organizational processes, and implement structures that support long-term integration across the space acquisition enterprise. Recognized for disciplined execution, strategic foresight, and continuous improvement in delivering mission-critical space capabilities. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): All new appointees to the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the five mandatory ECQs: ECQ 1. Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding: Demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2. Driving Efficiency: Demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3. Merit and Competence: Demonstrated knowledge, ability, and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4. Leading People: Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5. Achieving Results: Demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Please note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program, or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you must attach proof (e.g., SF-50 or Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.SubAgencyName: Office of the Assistant Secretary of the Air Force for Space Acquisition and Integration (SAF/SQ)
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is to fly, fight and win...airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Reach and Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do.
MajorDuties: The role oversees all financial, policy, and legislative activities for Space Force acquisitions, acting as a critical bridge between senior leadership, Congress, and Department of War stakeholders to ensure the rapid and effective delivery of space capabilities. The incumbent leads enterprise-level oversight of Space Force investment funding, managing Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) actions to ensure resources continuously support program execution and the rapid fielding of capabilities. This comprehensive oversight includes directing cost, schedule, and performance reporting, as well as managing Special Access Program (SAP) governance across the Department of War. To maintain portfolio health, the executive develops, codifies, and enforces space acquisition policies while supervising the acquisition review forums necessary for the Space Service Acquisition Executive to make critical development and production decisions. Beyond program and financial oversight, the position is responsible for driving enterprise integration and stakeholder alignment. The incumbent builds and leads teams focused on policy development and SAP oversight, fostering deep collaborative relationships across the Space Force Staff, Air Staff, Field Commands, and other DoW organizations. A core duty is ensuring that diverse stakeholder views are accurately synthesized and communicated to executive decision-makers, while simultaneously cultivating the personnel skills and organizational structures required for long-term space acquisition success. Furthermore, the executive serves as a senior advisor and primary external representative, providing technical assistance to the Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary for Congressional testimonies and inquiries. The incumbent maintains active liaisons with lawmakers and represents leadership in negotiations with the Office of the Secretary of War (OSW), other military departments, industry partners, foreign governments, and the Government Accountability Office (GAO). By formulating strategic policies and leading SAP legislative engagement, the executive works to build consensus, resolve cross-organizational conflicts, and support crisis management efforts.

Highly Qualified applicants may undergo one or more interviews and may be referred to the selecting official for further consideration. Upon selection, if not already a member of the SES serving under a career appointment, the selected candidate must have their executive qualifications certified by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualifications Review Board (QRB) prior to appointment. MatchedObjectDescriptor.OrganizationName: Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You may qualify at the GS-14, if you fulfill the following qualifications: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service: Performing advanced analysis in support of Joint Force development and design, assessing the effectiveness of programs, processes, and initiatives related to capability development, organizational performance, and mission execution; Applying advanced analytic tools and automation - including artificial intelligence, large language models, and other automation capabilities - to organize, evaluate, and derive insights from large volumes of structured and unstructured information to support joint concept implementation and capability development activities, identify gaps, compare alternatives, and develop recommendations to improve effectiveness, efficiency, and future force outcomes; Consolidating complex, ambiguous, and conflicting information into authoritative analysis while integrating knowledge of the Joint Warfighting Concept, policies, and objectives, to support force development, force design, and the integration of emerging technologies into future concepts; Developing executive-level staff products, including analytical reports, decision support materials, briefings, presentations, and recommendations, to inform senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders on Joint Force development, readiness, resilience, and adaptability; Supporting multidisciplinary efforts to design, enable, analyze, and document rigorous analytic and related capability development activities that accelerate Joint Warfighting Concept refinement and the integration of emerging technologies into future force design. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. This position serves as a senior analyst and Subject Matter Expert (SME) supporting the realization of the Department of War's (DoW) Joint Warfighting Concept and the delivery of required joint capabilities under the Joint Force Requirements Process (JFRP).
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: MISSION STATEMENT: Joint Staff J-7, in support of the Chairman, trains, educates, develops , designs and adapts the globally integrated, partnered joint force to achieve overmatch in the continuum of conflict in competition and crisis under conditions of accelerating change in the character of war.
MajorDuties: As a MANAGEMENT AND PROGRAM ANALYST (CAPABILITY DEVELOPMENT) at the GS-0343-14 some of your typical work assignments may include: Develops, leads, and conducts studies and comprehensive program management analysis to identify, frame, and prioritize the Department's most pressing JOPs and to evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of solution options across the doctrine, organization, training, material, leadership and education, personnel, facilities, and policy (DOTmLPF-P) spectrum Plans and conducts analytic efforts in support of Capability Portfolio Management (CPM) and Capability Portfolio Management Reviews (CPMRs) establishing problem framing, scope, and approach Integrates cross-domain solutions by relating capabilities, dependencies, and interoperability requirements across the DoW enterprise, identifying unwarranted duplication for potential divestment, and identifying opportunities to leverage the full defense enterprise - including Service programs, commercial innovation, science and technology efforts, and allied and partner contributions. Prepares J-7 senior leaders for participation in Functional Capabilities Board (FCB), Joint Capabilities Board (JCB), and Joint Requirements Oversight Council (JROC) fora, and represents the Division to boards and working groups composed of general officers, flag officers, and members of the Senior Executive Service

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is a Military Technician position with the 79th Sustainment Support Command, 419 Transportation Battalion, 649 Regional Support Group, 103 Expeditionary Sustainment Command that is located at Peoria, Illinois. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This is a military technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the better of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Provide advice regarding individual training requirements to management.
Ensure training requirements are met through coordination with management.
Compose reports on the standing of program requirements.
Evaluate regulations for required changes in training programs.
Conduct inspections to ensure compliance with organizational inspection program.

You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: providing administrative assistance in support of a military unit or military activity in one or more of the following areas: unit or individual training, medical readiness, personnel actions, financial actions, supply, or logistics; performing day-to-day administrative functions; and preparing or reviewing written products. OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Organizational Management and Leadership, Public Administration, Business Administration, and Management. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Military Technician position with the 377th Theater Sustainment Command, 839th Transportation Detachment, 332nd Transportation Battalion, 641st Regional Support Group, 143rd Expeditionary Sustainment Command located in Perrine, Florida. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This is a Military Technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician Program. This enables you to receive full Civil Service benefits and full Military Reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserve and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Manage the daily operations of a US Army Reserve unit’s mission readiness program.
Represent the US Army Reserve Troop Program Unit Commander in his/her absence.
Perform as the record manager.
Serve as the unit physical security coordinator.
Review regulations and directives and implements changes in appropriate manner.
Compile data and create products to present at briefings.
Prepare and review command correspondence for content and accuracy.
Manage unit and individual personnel and medical readiness.
Execute the unit’s supply and logistics program.
Coordinate the management of unit and individual training readiness.
Administer financial management program including Government Purchasing and Travel Card programs.
Advise on pay, benefits, entitlements, incentives, and assist with correcting pay issues.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT: The employee may be recalled to duty, may be required to work other than normal duty hours, which may include evening, weekends, and/or holidays, and may be required to work overtime. In the performance of assigned duties, employee uses tact, diplomacy, and professionalism to promote effective working relationships with a variety of offices and agencies. YA002 = Eligible for situational telework only, including Ad hoc, Emergency, or OPM prescribed "Unscheduled" Telework. This eligibility is separate and distinct from the employee's eligibility. A civilian employee's telework arrangement may be terminated at the discretion of the supervisor or at the employee's request. Performs additional duties as assigned. In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-12, or equivalent in other pay systems. Example of specialized experience includes: (1) Utilizing the current missions, capabilities, organization and operations involving federal interagency and multinational organizations; (2) applying analytical and evaluative methods and techniques to complex issues concerning the efficiency and effectiveness of the Joint Training Program; (3) exercising pertinent laws, regulations, policies and precedents; (4) providing local, state, and federal agencies organization, structure and plans as related to homeland defense, homeland security, crisis management, and consequence management, civil disturbance, etc., as well as a master level understanding of highly classified global campaign and operational plans; and (5) working with current military law, joint doctrine, joint plans, policies, and practices. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-12 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-13 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Skill in the management of detailed planning and execution of multiple exercises. Knowledge of foreign disclosure, security policies and procedures. 2. Knowledge of the functions, goals, objectives, and work processes pertinent to conducting Combatant Command and Bi-national Command training exercises. 3. Knowledge of current military law, national strategy, national response framework, joint plans, policies, plans and guidance. Skill in managing several projects simultaneously. 4. Skill in applying Joint Training System concepts to meet exercise and training objectives and reporting responsibilities. Skill in leading exercise planning events, to negotiate and defend ideas and support exercise concepts. 5. Knowledge of crisis response processes and the command and controls systems. 6. Skill in written and oral communication. Skills in the preparation of broad and difficult comprehensive management studies to propose solutions to challenging management problems. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MajorDuties: Responsible for the development of CCMD-level policy for all aspects of VIGILANT SHIELD, VITAL ARCHER, ARDENT SENTRY, and/or NUWAIX. Contributes to the development of policy by scheduling, resourcing, planning, designing, developing and executing exercises for NORAD and USNORTHCOM. Establishes, maintains, and executes the exercise planning schedule for the Commands' Tier 1 and Tier 2, JEP-designated exercises and all linked and associated exercises, to include scheduling all conferences, meetings, in-progress reviews, and secure video teleconferences. Coordinates with NORAD and USNORTHCOM senior staff, and various levels of other participating external agencies to schedule and organize numerous exercise events. As a NORAD and USNORTHCOM Domain Exercise Controller of the Joint Exercise Control Group (JECG), acts as a key domain exercise observer/controller, managing and directing, up to 200, co-located and geographically dispersed binational personnel during NORAD and USNORTHCOM exercises and other supported Joint and Combined exercises. Controls exercise activities and vignette/scenario injects, to include de-confliction; ensures training objectives are met, provides guidance to participants, and briefs the Director, Joint Training and Exercises, Chief, Joint Exercise Division and the Senior JECG Director on domain specific status of the exercise.
Details.Education: This job does not have an education qualification requirement or applicable education substitution for experience. ********************ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FOR ACTIVE DUTY SERVICES MEMBERS******************** ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act requires federal agencies to treat an eligible active duty service member as a veteran, disabled veteran, and preference eligible (as applicable) when applying for civil service positions before the effective release or discharge date. Appointment of military members before the release or discharge date is permissible if the member is on terminal leave. At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD-Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD-Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. The certification memo must originate from the member's military service branch on official letterhead and contain the following: Name/Rank/Grade of Service Member Branch of Armed Forces Dates of Active Service (Start and End Date(s) Expected Date of Discharge/Release from Active Duty Terminal leave start date (if applicable) Expected character of service (honorable or general) and type of separation (i.e. separation or retirement) Must be certified within 120 days of anticipated discharge Signature by, or by direction of the adjutant, personnel office, unit commander, or higher headquarters commander. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form-214 must be submitted upon receipt

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Conditions of Employment CONT: May be required to perform Battle Roster functions during Exercises and Real-World events. Battle Roster functions may include but are not limited to the Joint Operations Center (JOC), Future Operations Center (FOC), Future Plans Center (FPC), Joint Logistics Operations Center (JLOC), N&NC Deployment and Distribution Operations Center (NDDOC), Joint Intelligence Operations Center-North (JIOC-N), Joint Cyber Center (JCC), and other tasks as assigned. These duties may require additional duty hours and/or a physical/medical assessment to deploy to alternate duty locations (non-combat) or inplace. The physical/medical assessment is not a pre-employment requirement. This is a KEY position IAW 32 CFR, Part 44 Appendix A and DoD Directive 1200.7. A Key Position is a Federal position that cannot be vacated during a war, national emergency, or mobilization without seriously impairing the capability of the parent Federal Agency to function effectively. Applicants for positions designated as "Key" positions who do not agree to this condition shall not be extended an offer of employment. The employee must be removed from the Ready Reserve and CANNOT become a member of the Ready Reserve while assigned to this position. IAW DoDI 3020-42 this position has been locally, or command designated as Mission Essential (ME). ME personnel perform a Mission Critical Function (MCF), which must continue uninterrupted after the occurrence of an emergency or during hazardous weather conditions to keep critical operations functioning. These personnel are required to report for duty at normal times when the base is closed or if delayed reporting is directed and remain on duty during phased or early release. In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-12, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes: (1) Working knowledge of joint and combined planning processes, COCOM Command campaign and contingency planning constructs, and associated doctrine, policy, and guidance to translate broad national- and joint-level direction into executable plans, lines of effort, and decision options; (2) Working with complex strategic planning and analysis to translate broad national-level and COCOM Command-level guidance into integrated plans, concepts, and courses of action; and (3) Working with managing the full life cycle of complex projects, including defining scope, developing project plans, managing milestones and risks, integrating inputs, and delivering decision-quality products on time. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-12 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-13 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Ability to perform complex strategic planning and analysis to translate broad national-level and CCMD-level guidance into integrated plans, concepts, and courses of action. Skill in managing the full life cycle of complex projects, including defining scope, developing project plans, managing milestones and risks, integrating inputs, and delivering decision-quality products on time. Ability to conduct rigorous qualitative and quantitative analysis of incomplete or ambiguous information to identify trends, assess risks and opportunities, and develop feasible, distinguishable options and recommendations. Skill in building and sustaining effective working relationships with diverse internal and external stakeholders to gather information, align efforts, and integrate products across organizational boundaries. Ability to communicate complex strategic and analytical information clearly and persuasively in writing, including preparing decision papers, options analyses, executive summaries, and related documentation for senior leaders. Skill in delivering concise, well-organized briefings and presentations that explain complex issues, findings, and recommendations to senior officials and other audiences. Ability to evaluate and improve planning, project management, and coordination processes by identifying gaps or friction points and recommending practical improvements, tools, or methods that enhance the quality and timeliness of outputs. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: Click on "Learn more about this agency" button below to view Eligibilities being considered and other IMPORTANT information. The primary purpose of this position: To serve as a strategic planner in the Commanders' Initiative Group (CIG), NORAD and USNORTHCOM (N/NC), responsible for planning, managing, and executing complex Combatant Command (CCMD)-level initiatives and analytic projects that support senior leader decision making.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: US Northern Command (USNORTHCOM) Mission Statement: Conduct operations to deter, prevent, and defeat threats and aggression aimed at the United States, its territories, and interests within the assigned area of responsibility; and as directed by the President or Secretary of Defense, provide defense support of civil authorities including consequence management operations. Find out more click here. MajorDuties: Performs advanced strategic planning, analysis, and command messaging to support NORAD and USNORTHCOM senior leader decision making. Plans, organizes, and manages complex strategic initiatives and analytic projects across the full life cycle to deliver decision-quality products. Integrates strategic planning and analytic efforts with headquarters, joint, interagency, and bi-national activities and improves related processes and information flows. Performs senior-level strategic analysis and staff support and carries out ancillary duties that contribute to CIG and N/NC missions.
Details.Education: ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act requires federal agencies to treat an eligible active duty service member as a veteran, disabled veteran, and preference eligible (as applicable) when applying for civil service positions before the effective release or discharge date. Appointment of military members before the release or discharge date is permissible if the member is on terminal leave. At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD-Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD-Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. The certification memo must originate from the member's military service branch on official letterhead and contain the following: Name/Rank/Grade of Service Member Branch of Armed Forces Dates of Active Service (Start and End Date(s) Expected Date of Discharge/Release from Active Duty Terminal leave start date (if applicable) Expected character of service (honorable or general) and type of separation (i.e. separation or retirement) Must be certified within 120 days of anticipated discharge Signature by, or by direction of the adjutant, personnel office, unit commander, or higher headquarters commander. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form-214 must be submitted upon receipt

Your qualifications will be evaluated based on your application materials (e.g., resume, supporting documents), your responses on the application questionnaire, and your responses to all assessments required for this position. You will be assessed on the following competencies (knowledge, skills, abilities, and other characteristics) Judgement, Reasoning, Occupational and Reading The resume/documents you submit must support your responses to the online questionnaire. If your application contradicts or does not support your questionnaire responses, you will receive a rating of "not qualified" or "insufficient information" and you will not receive further consideration for this job. Please follow all instructions carefully. Errors or omissions may affect your rating or consideration for employment. Current Federal Civilian employees should list any relevant performance related rating and/or awards in your resume. Additional points are not added for Veteran's Preference; however, Veteran's Preference is considered where applicable. Best Qualified Group: Candidates in this category possess exceptional skills and experience to exceed well above the minimum requirements Fully Qualified Group: Candidates in this category possess good skills and experience above the minimum requirements. Basically Qualified Group: Candidates in this category meet the minimum education and/or experience requirements. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-11, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes knowledge of a wide variety of CBRN, emergency management concepts, principles, practices, laws, and regulations to plan, organize, direct, operate, and evaluate an emergency management program for a large integrating mutual support from but not limited to communities, states, and counties. Knowledge and understanding of the current missions, capabilities, organization and operations of: USNORTHCOM; other unified commands; the military services; the National Guard; the Reserve forces; DoD; DHS, FEMA, the US Coast Guard, and other Interagency organizations. Knowledge of military command structures, missions, programs, and organizational relationships and program goals and objectives, the sequence and timing of key operational events and milestones, and methods of evaluating the effectiveness of planning actions as related to actual events. Skill in both written and oral communication; negotiating complex issues; and maintaining good working relations. Ability to staff/coordinate packages within the Command and other agencies. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-11 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-12 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of CBRN Consequence Management operations and planning. Knowledge of management principles and processes to sequence key operational events and meet program milestones; methods of evaluating the effectiveness of planning actions related to actual events; and the relationship of the various command entities involved in overall program planning and execution of military operations and evaluations. Skill in designing and conducting comprehensive evaluations, after-action reviews, and related products in order to prepare solutions to resolve substantive problems and issues of effectiveness and efficiency of work operations in a major command program. Skill in both written and oral communication. Skill in negotiating complex issues. Skill in maintaining good working relations. Ability to participate in study teams; originate new ideas, projects, and methodologies; and execute projects and/or studies within established constraints. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: IMPORTANT INFORMATION: This Job Opportunity Announcement (JOA) will be used to form a pool of qualified applicants who will be considered for direct hire vacancies as they become available. To learn more about the United States Space Force Mission click here
MajorDuties: The United States Space Force (USSF) Peterson SFB, Colorado Springs, CO is searching for an International & Spectrum Engagement Manager (NH-0346-03, GS 12/13 equivalent). *Position is eligible to be filled at either Peterson Space Force Base Colorado Springs, CO or Los Angeles Space Force Base, El Segundo CA* Description: The US Space Force is seeking a dynamic and strategic leader to manage the enterprise intake process for external stakeholders, focusing on international/allied integration and complex regulatory deconfliction. In this high-impact role, you will serve as the primary liaison guiding foreign partners and commercial entities through the bureaucratic, technical, and regulatory requirements necessary to connect to the US Space Force satellite communication network. You will direct the onboarding intake funnel-framing collaboration through established tiered opportunities such as federated network or industrial partnerships-while standardizing processes to minimize friction and ensure capabilities are technically and administratively aligned before production handoff. To ensure global operational readiness, you will navigate, expedite, and manage long-lead regulatory and spectrum licensing processes required for new antenna providers and global operation centers. This position requires exceptional strategic decision support, analytical acumen, superior time management, and highly polished written and oral communication skills to coordinate seamlessly with host nations, major commands, and international directorates to align allied integration with broader US Space Force strategies. Ideal Candidate: An ideal candidate for this US Space Force position will possess a strong academic foundation, holding a bachelor's degree in international relations, Public Policy, National Security, Engineering, or a business/analytical field, with a master's degree preferred, or equivalent specialized military experience. They must exhibit high proficiency in navigating complex, long-lead licensing requirements, particularly through direct coordination with the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA), Federal Communications Commission (FCC), and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). This role demands robust analytical skills to successfully balance stringent security controls with critical operational timelines. Key Skills and Abilities: 1. Knowledge of the applicable principles, concepts, policies, and laws; functions, programs, and systems applicable to the duties of logistics contracts and program management and material support; sources, responsibilities, and means for providing assistance and advice to resolve logistics contracts and program management problems; and all aspects of logistics contracts and program management support. 2. Knowledge of government and private industry policies and practices related to business management, industrial management, financial systems, technical concepts, and production practices. Ability to gather, analyze, and evaluate a variety of program information, such as commercial business practices, market conditions, offer acceptability, contractor acceptability, contractor responsibility and/or performance to determine acquisition strategy and sources. 3. Knowledge of the missions, roles, functions, organizational structures, and operation of the Department of Defense and entities that govern, interface with, and/or influence management control of proposed and ongoing service contracts. 4. Knowledge of methods of supervision to hold others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions of a unit and mentor, motivate, and appraise subordinate staff. Determine objectives, make sound, well-informed, and objective decisions, set priorities, cause change, and accomplish organizational goals. 5. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, clearly, concisely, with technical accuracy and to use computers and a variety of software programs and databases, gather and analyze a variety of program information progress. 6. Ability to establish and maintain good relationships with individuals and groups within the office as well as outside the immediate work unit and to be persuasive in representing the best interests of the government when dealing with personnel with highly divergent points of view. 7. Ability to plan, organize, analyze problems, translate complex information, make appropriate judgments, evaluate options, conduct research, summarize results, make appropriate recommendations, and manage critical aspects of service contract requirements as related to the assigned functional area and meet deadlines. Ability to compose and edit contract required correspondence, review and analyze directives, develop and brief service contract program related presentations.

Details.JobSummary: About the position: This position will be assigned to the Peterson Hub located on Peterson Space Force Base. Position is a position of trust. This position may require shift work to provide coverage on evenings, weekends, holidays, or special situations.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Thank you for considering employment with Air Force Services Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF). Peterson SFB is located just south of Colorado Springs at the base of the Rocky Mountains. The unparalleled beauty and mild climate of Colorado Springs make it a gateway to a wide variety of outdoor activities. Many internationally known ski areas and some of the nation's most scenic parks and finest hunting and fishing areas are located within a short drive. Peterson SFB Families have easy access to the many cultural attractions of "The Springs" and the bright lights of nearby Denver.
MajorDuties: Duties and Responsibilities: Applying knowledge of the organization, its functions, and regulations, the incumbent of the position carries out a wide variety of event programming duties related to the Force Support Squadron organization and its mission. Plans and coordinates the day-to-day administrative and operational activities of a narrowly defined set of funded activities within the Peterson Hub. The program/project is usually focused to a single purpose or service oriented and may exist as a subset of an integrated program activity. Duties typically include the planning and administration of events, budget, and/or other associated transactions for program implementation and administration; incumbent is the operational/administrative liaison of program marketing and reporting of the Hub's event functions. Provides specialized administrative support in the development, implementation, and marketing of program/project function. Works closely with the Food and Beverage Manager and Catering Support Coordinator on day-to-day programmatic, operational, and administrative matters related to the fulfillment of the organization's mission. Plans and coordinates the details for recurring and non­recurring activities for the HUB Events Program, as to make maximum use of the facilities, services, and other resources. Events include: Hub activities, base picnics, and in-brief socials, icebreakers receptions for evaluation teams, military and civilian ceremonies and other related events and programs. Coordinates activities of support staff engaging in the implementation and administration of program objectives. Follows up the reviewing and consolidating of after-action reports and submits recommendations to Hub management. Coordinates with Marketing Director the necessary publicity and sponsorship projects in support of HUB events. Solicits paid entertainment and various other resources in support of events. Establishes necessary budgets and coordinates with appropriate contacts to secure funding. Accounts for funds received and expended, and makes recommendations to supervisor for improvements in funding additional personnel, supplies, equipment, and facilities to operate or promote special event activities and programs. Plans, coordinates, and participates in event set-up and tear down duties. May perform other related duties as assigned. Position is a position of trust. Performs other related duties as assigned. As a mandatory requirement for employment in this TDP, the incumbent is (A) to refrain from use of illegal drugs and (B) if required, to submit to urinalysis testing. Illegal drug use by employees in sensitive position presents a clear threat to the mission of the Air Force, national security, and public safety. The selectee must sign a statement acknowledging the position occupied is identified as a TDP. May be required to perform Battle Roster functions during Exercises and Real-World events. Battle Roster functions may include but are not limited to the Joint Operations Center (JOC), Future Operations Center (FOC), Future Plans Center (FPC), Joint Logistics Operations Center (JLOC), N&NC Deployment and Distribution Operations Center (NDDOC), Joint Intelligence Operations Center-North (JIOC-N), Joint Cyber Center (JCC), and other tasks as assigned. These duties may require additional duty hours and/or a physical/medical assessment to deploy to alternate duty locations (non-combat) or in-place. The physical/medical assessment is not a pre-employment requirement. This is a KEY position IAW 32 CFR, Part 44 Appendix A and DOD Directive 1200.7. A Key Position is a Federal position that cannot be vacated during a war, national emergency, or mobilization without seriously impairing the capability of the parent Federal Agency to function effectively. Applicants for positions designated as "Key" positions who do not agree to this condition shall not be extended an offer of employment. The employee must be removed from the Ready Reserve and CANNOT become a member of the Ready Reserve while assigned to this position. YA002 = Eligible for situational telework only, including Ad hoc, Emergency, or OPM prescribed "Unscheduled" Telework. This eligibility is separate and distinct from the employee's eligibility. A civilian employee's telework arrangement may be terminated at the discretion of the supervisor or at the employee's request. In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions, Miscellaneous Administration and Program Series 0301. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-12, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes SME knowledge and understanding of military strategic, operational, and tactical concepts, principles, and processes in all dimensions of MA to provide senior leadership with advisory services and recommendations. Requisite knowledge of current military law, Joint doctrine, Joint plans, policies, and practice, as well as understanding of US government treaties, agreements, multi-lateral and bi-lateral international agreements, U.S. security requirements and arrangements, and other pertinent laws, doctrine, policies, and procedures. The position requires the incumbent to perform at a combatant command level in support of DOD Homeland Defense (HD), and Defense Support to Civil Authorities (DSCA) operations and planning. Practical and professional knowledge of a wide range of Services technical methods, principles, and practices. Thorough knowledge of interagency organizations such as DHS CISA, the National Infrastructure Coordination Center (NICC), and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to perform reviews and coordinate the integration of NORAD & USNORTHCOM plans, policies, and exercises. Mastery of a wide range of DCI and civilian infrastructure disciplines, concepts, principles, practices, programs and requirements as well as broad knowledge of DOD MA protection programs, activities, and planning. Knowledge and experience at the installation, intermediate Command and Unified Command levels in MA risk management. Knowledge and background to provide advice and recommendations to the Joint Staff, Services, DOD Agencies and Component Commands on MA risk management and DCI and support CI protection in support of HD and DSCA. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-12 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-13 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge and skill in facilitating processes and procedures for dealing with a wide range of emergency situations impacting DCI and supporting CI that conceivably retain strategic and national level significance. Knowledge of the roles and organization of the Services and combatants, unified, and multi-national commands, and involved federal, state and local agencies as they apply to risk management of impacting DCI and supporting CI. Knowledge of military law and doctrine, Joint policies and procedures, DOD, Services and Joint organizational structures, national intelligence organizations, state and federal emergency organizations, other pertinent interagency organizations such as those embedded within the DHS. Ability to analyze information, reach appropriate conclusions, and effectively resolves problems in DCI and supporting CI area. Ability to identify customer needs, tailor plans and strategies, and implement actions within established policies. Skilled in articulating MA and related protection programs and activities, procedures, and policies clearly and concisely in written and oral formats. Skilled in the application of methods and techniques to analyze and evaluate the effects of changes in MA related plans and funding. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MajorDuties: The primary purpose of this position is: To serve as a Mission Assurance (MA) Operations Specialist assessing risk to the North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD) and United States Northern Command (USNORTHCOM) critical mission capabilities utilizing the Department of Defense (DOD) MA Construct and its associated protection programs and activities. The MA Operations Specialist, in collaboration with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Critical Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), is at the forefront of USNORTHCOMs ability to execute the MA Construct by assessing all Threats and Hazards and protecting the homeland through the identification, prioritization, assessment, mitigation, remediation, and management ofrisk to Defense Critical Infrastructure (DCI) in the USNORTHCOM Area of Responsibility (AOR). Duties: Serves as a MA Operations Specialist performing reviews and coordinating the integration of NORAD & USNORTHCOM plans, policies, and exercises with all DOD entities within the AOR. Serves as a command operational SME on MA risk management and related protection activities supporting the MA Branch, Protection, and MA Division, NCJ34. Serves as a MA Watch stander on the deployable mobile command center providing 24/7 support in assessing and managing risk to NORAD & USNORTHCOM and DOD critical missions. Serves as the SME for MA risk management functions and principles as they apply to MA and DCI assessment.

MajorDuties: You will oversee the organization's strategic plan, schedule, budget management planning, reporting and execution of the authority for construction, outfitting, and test of the Motor Module activities as delegated by PMS397.

You will coach the team in the selection and application of problem solving methods and techniques, provide advice on work methods, practices and procedures, and assist the team in identifying the parameters of a viable solution.
You will lead the team in identifying, distributing and balancing workload and tasks among employees in accordance with established work flow, skill level and occupational specialization.
You will monitor and report on the status and progress of work to see that the supervisor's instructions on work priorities, methods, deadlines and quality have been met.
You will monitor EBC's program performance and progress regarding cost, schedule and scope.

You will review and analyze all formal documentation associated with the Motor Module detail design, construction and test phases, and of comparable documentation for design support contracts, and related programs.
You will review EB generated Change Notification Reports (CN), Problem Sheets (PS) and respective level of Assembly (LOA) for overall design and production engineering impact and action.

Drug-Free Workplace Policy The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is committed to maintaining a safe, drug-free workplace. All DLA employees are required to refrain from illegal drug use on and off duty. DLA conducts pre-employment, reasonable suspicion, post-accident, and random drug testing. Applicants tentatively selected for employment in testing designated positions will undergo a urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Refusal to undergo testing or testing positive for illegal drugs will result in withdrawal of the tentative job offer and a six-month denial of employment with DLA from the date of the drug test. Employees in drug testing designated positions are subject to random drug testing. A negative drug test result must be received by HR within 30 calendar days after the EOD (i.e., start date). The selectee's inability successfully pass; or refusal to conduct the test may result in: 1) the tentative or FJO being withdrawn during the recruitment process; or 2) subsequently being removed from Federal service for failure to meet a condition of employment. You may be required to sign a "Drug Test Statement of Understanding" if you are selected for this position. The DLA drug testing panel tests for the following substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates, heroin, phencyclidine, amphetamines, methamphetamines, fentanyl, norfentanyl, methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), and opioids. ADVISORY: Use of cannabidiol (CBD) products may result in a positive drug test for marijuana. DLA employees are subject to Federal law and under Federal law, Marijuana is illegal. Applicants tentatively selected for employment in testing designated positions will undergo a urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Refusal to undergo testing or testing positive for illegal drugs will result in withdrawal of the tentative job offer and a six-month denial of employment with DLA from the date of the drug test. Employees in drug testing designated positions are subject to random drug testing. A negative drug test result must be received by HR within 30 calendar days after the EOD (i.e., start date). The selectee's inability successfully pass; or refusal to conduct the test may result in: 1) the tentative or FJO being withdrawn during the recruitment process; or 2) subsequently being removed from Federal service for failure to meet a condition of employment. You may be required to sign a "Drug Test Statement of Understanding" if you are selected for this position. The DLA drug testing panel tests for the following substances: marijuana, cocaine, opiates, heroin, phencyclidine, amphetamines, methamphetamines, fentanyl, norfentanyl, methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), methylenedioxyamphetamine (MDA), and opioids. ADVISORY: Use of cannabidiol (CBD) products may result in a positive drug test for marijuana. DLA employees are subject to Federal law and under Federal law, Marijuana is illegal. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify for a Management Analyst your resume and supporting documentation must support: A. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience that equipped you with the particular competencies to successfully perform the duties of the position and is directly in or related to this position. To qualify at the GS-09 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military, or private sector. Applicants must meet eligibility requirements including time-in-grade (General Schedule (GS) positions only), time-after-competitive appointment, minimum qualifications, and any other regulatory requirements by the cut-off/closing date of the announcement. Creditable specialized experience includes: Gathering, reviewing, preparing and consolidating a variety of statistical data and narrative justifications for the fiscal year's resource requirements for travel, training, awards, base operating supplies, equipment rental, subscriptions, impress funds, and personnel. Determining Directorate training requirements based on specific requests, mission priority, program requirements, and developmental needs of new personnel as well as coordinating training requirements with the Management Planning Office and the Office of Human Resources (OHR). Providing administrative support functions for Director/Deputy including preparation of draft replies to congressional and other high-level correspondence; as necessary, arranges for replies by other Directorate officials coordinating reply with staff offices ensuring timely response by DSCP Command. B. Education Substitution: Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work. Education must be from a college or university accredited by an organization approved by the U.S. Department of Education. See http://ope.ed.gov/accreditation/Search.aspx. If using education to meet basic qualifications, YOU MUST SUBMIT A TRANSCRIPT as supplemental documentation. To qualify based on education in lieu of specialized experience, you must possess: A master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B. or J.D., if related. C. Combination: Combinations of successfully completed post-high school education and experience may be used to meet total qualification requirements for grade levels GS-09 and may be computed by first determining the applicant's total qualifying experience as a percentage of the experience required for the grade level; then determining the applicant's education as a percentage of the education required for the grade level; and then adding the two percentages. The total percentages must equal at least 100 percent to qualify an applicant for that grade level. Only graduate education in excess of the amount required for the next lower grade level may be used to qualify applicants for positions at grade GS-09. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Military Technician position with the Military Intelligence Readiness Command, Company C, 301 Military Intelligence Battalion, 259th Expeditionary Military Intelligence Brigade (E-MIB) located in Phoenix, Arizona. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This is a military technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the better of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Provide guidance to personnel on changes to organizational regulations and directives.
Utilize various automation systems to identify financial management program deficiencies.
Analyze account report system to maintain inventory.
Coordinate training programs for personnel in accordance with organizational directives and guidance.
Manage the travel program for the organization.
Provide pay guidance to organizational personnel.
Perform daily administrative functions in support of the organization’s readiness program.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This is a Military Technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician Program. This enables you to receive full Civil Service benefits and full Military Reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserve and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Perform daily administrative functions in support of the organization’s readiness program.

Analyze account report system to maintain inventory.
Coordinate training programs for personnel in accordance with organizational directives and guidance.
Manage the travel program for the organization.
Provide pay guidance to organizational personnel.

MajorDuties: THIS IS A T5 EXCEPTED SERVICE, PERMANENT POSITION. The primary purpose of the UNIT DEPLOYMENT MANAGER, GS-0301-9, is to function as the Unit Deployment Manager (UDM), responsible for executing, coordinating, and overseeing all aspects of personnel and equipment readiness and deployment planning in support of Air Force Force Generation (AFFORGEN) requirements. Coordinates movement with Installation Deployment Officer (IDO) and Traffic Management Flight for Air Force Force Generation (AFFORGEN). Manages unit readiness reporting through the Defense Readiness Reporting System (DRRS). Manages unit deployment operations in coordination with the Installation Deployment Readiness Center. Monitors readiness using the AFFORGEN-Connect Commanders Toolkit and Military Personnel Data System. Maintains electronic Deployment Readiness Checklists (e-DRCs) and Air Force Deployment Folders(e-AFDFs). Conducts reviews and ensures checklist accuracy. Provides technical guidance to leadership on unit deployment capabilities. Advises the commander on tasking response, shortfall mitigation, and application of deployment policies. Interprets Joint, Air Force, and MAJCOM planning guidance and briefs leadership on applicable requirements. Develops workload mitigation plans to maximize deployable capability. Evaluates Unit Type Code (UTC) package composition and recommends changes based on unit capability. The position resides within the infrastructure and support functions of the state National Guard; the incumbent is not subject to mobilization, nor is the work described part of the military mission; and the incumbent does not perform a key advisory or essential administrative role that is inherently military. In addition, the position must meet one of the following: It does not have a comparable military function; the position is required in full-time (civilian) role when the organization, or similar military position, is mobilized to perform continuing post-mobilization functions; or the position requires a skill or competency that necessitates technical expertise or professional qualifications that cannot be readily found in the military structure of the state military force. May make additional selections within 90 days of eligible(s) issuance.
