MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. 30 Percent or More Disabled Veterans Current Department of Army Civilian Employees Current Department of Defense (DOD) Civilian Employee (non-Army) Executive Order (E.O.) 12721 Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Non-Appropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) Non-Department of Defense (DoD) Transfer Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Interchange Agreement Eligible People with Disabilities, Schedule A Postal Service/Peace Corps and Other Unique Authorities Reinstatement Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA) of 1998 Veterans Recruitment Appointment (VRA) In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes:1) providing administrative assistance support in one or more of the following areas: training, medical readiness, personnel actions, financial actions, supply, or logistics; 2) coordinate logistical and training support with internal personnel and/or organizations; and 3) prepare various written correspondence to be briefed to organizational personnel. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Business Administration, Strategic Management and Organizational Design and Development. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. (Note: You must attach a copy of your transcripts.) Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-07).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a military technician position with the 377th Theater Sustainment Command, 1173 Deployment Distribution Support Battalion, 1189 Transportation Support Brigade, Deployment Support Command located at West Palm Beach, Florida. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This is a military technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician Program. This enables you to receive full Civil Service benefits and full Military Reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserve and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Perform daily administrative functions in support of the organization’s readiness program.
Provide guidance to personnel on changes to organizational regulations and directives.
Utilize various automation systems to identify financial management program deficiencies.
Analyze account report system to maintain inventory.
Coordinate training programs for personnel in accordance with organizational directives and guidance.
Manage the travel program for the organization.
Provide pay guidance to organizational personnel.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At West Point Family and MWR, our mission is to enhance the quality of life for Soldiers, Families, and the entire West Point community by delivering exceptional programs, services, and facilities. We are committed to fostering leadership, wellness, and connection through innovative recreation, dining, and special events that reflect the unique spirit of West Point. Join us in creating a vibrant and supportive environment where excellence thrives. Located in the scenic Hudson River Valley, only 50 miles from New York City, the U.S. Military Academy at West Point is a four-year academic institution, a nationally-renowned historic site, and the oldest continuously occupied military post in America. West Point's 3,000 civilian employees have access to Eisenhower Hall Theatre, the Hudson Valley's premier performing arts center, and recreational facilities such as an 18-hole Golf Course and Ski Slope.
MajorDuties: Manages, schedules and executes work to accomplish banquet events. Creates room diagrams for planned events.
Assigns work to subordinate staff in setting up of attractive, creative, and imaginative buffet tables and ensures duties are completed as required within budget parameters for event.

Performs client contact during functions, monitors satisfaction, last minute changes and special requests; reports all pertinent information to the supervisor and recommends operational improvements as necessary for future events.
Performs the full range of supervisory functions to include hiring, training, performance evaluation, recommends reward and recognition, discipline, work and leave schedules.
Oversight of catering fleet of vehicles.

Details.Benefits: Working for Army Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF) can offer numerous advantages. Army NAF employment can provide a sense of pride and fulfillment, as you'll be supporting communities comprised of military and civilian personnel, and their families, which contributes to the Department of Defense's overall mission. We offer a wide range of career opportunities, including jobs in childcare, recreation, hospitality, and more. Many employees have opportunities for professional development, including training, education, and certification programs to help towards career advancement. As an Army NAF employee, you'll have access to some on-base facilities, including fitness centers, libraries, and many other amenities. Regular full-time and part-time employees are eligible for enrollment in health and life insurance, participation in 401k and retirement plans, and paid personal time off and federal holidays. NAF flexible employees, working in the United States or a U.S. citizen or spouse or child of a U.S. citizen working for a NAFI in a foreign area, are eligible to participate in the NAF 401(k) plan. Some flexible employees may also be eligible to receive health insurance. For a slideshow presentation regarding these benefits, please click the Review Our Benefits link below.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At West Point Family and MWR, our mission is to enhance the quality of life for Soldiers, Families, and the entire West Point community by delivering exceptional programs, services, and facilities. We are committed to fostering leadership, wellness, and connection through innovative recreation, dining, and special events that reflect the unique spirit of West Point. Join us in creating a vibrant and supportive environment where excellence thrives. Located in the scenic Hudson River Valley, only 50 miles from New York City, the U.S. Military Academy at West Point is a four-year academic institution, a nationally-renowned historic site, and the oldest continuously occupied military post in America. West Point's 3,000 civilian employees have access to Eisenhower Hall Theatre, the Hudson Valley's premier performing arts center, and recreational facilities such as an 18-hole Golf Course and Ski Slope.
MajorDuties: Responsible for the management, supervision and service of all meetings, banquets, and catered functions in conjunction with the goals and tasks set forth for the Catering Department.
Directs and supervises catering staff in service standards and policies. Ensures security, maintenance and inventory of all catering and meeting equipment.

Handles banquet charges at the conclusion of catered functions for prompt and accurate accounting of all Catering department revenue and expenses. Ensures security, maintenance and inventory of all catering and meeting equipment.
Develop and execute strategic sales programs for catering within MWR facilities, ensuring alignment with sales objectives and the implementation of effective marketing and promotional plans.
Represent catering and build strong relationships with key clients, including military and civilian personnel.

Details.Benefits: Working for Army Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF) can offer numerous advantages. Army NAF employment can provide a sense of pride and fulfillment, as you'll be supporting communities comprised of military and civilian personnel, and their families, which contributes to the Department of Defense's overall mission. Resumes should clearly demonstrate the applicant's relevant experience, skills, knowledge and abilities as they pertain to this position. A qualified candidate must possess the following: 1. One (1) year of specialized work experience coordinating the various (operational requirements and functions) associated with Army Athletic Association (AAA) such as: planning and management, business planning, training administration, internal control, public relations, inspections, evaluation, and liaison activities. 2. Located in the scenic Hudson River valley, only 50 miles from New York City, the U.S. Military Academy at West Point is a four-year academic institution, a nationally-renowned historic site, and the oldest continuously occupied military post in America. Maintains liaison with USCC, other USMA and West Point Directorates and Departments, higher headquarters, other commands, other government agencies, and installations, to provide required support to Army Athletic Association related issues.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience. Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes 1) evaluating engineering, facility, infrastructure, or similar support programs; 2) identifying problems, trends, and gaps; 3) providing leadership with program status updates; 4) coordinating with higher headquarters or other stakeholders on changing requirements; and 5) monitoring complex projects or program actions across multiple offices or organizations to keep work on schedule, resolve issues, avoid duplicated effort, and meet requirements. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-12).

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Directs and evaluates Facilities and Infrastructure Program activities; analyzes program performance, proposals, and emerging requirements; and provides recommendations, alternative courses of action, and expert policy advice to senior leadership.

Manages and integrates assigned facilities and infrastructure projects to ensure timely execution, continuity of operations, resolution of deficiencies, and compliance with organizational requirements.

Coordinates with U.S. Army Hawaii, higher headquarters, installations, Joint Service organizations, and external agencies to synchronize infrastructure priorities, pending mandates, and strategic initiatives affecting U.S. Army Garrison Hawaii.

Serves as staff action officer for facilities and infrastructure matters; prepares correspondence, information papers, fact sheets, reports, studies, and briefings; and leads the coordination, staffing, tracking, and follow-up of assigned actions.

Conducts program evaluations, inspections, and staff assistance visits to assess compliance with program policies and plans, determine whether mandatory requirements are met, and evaluate Directorate and garrison program delivery.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: THIS IS AN AIR RESERVE TECHNICIAN OFFICER POSITION. This is an Air Reserve Technician (ART) Officer position located at 442 FIGHTER WG with the military rank of O-6/COL, AFSC: 091W0. For questions concerning military eligibility please contact the Air Force Reserve Qualification Center at 1-800-257-1212. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Three years of progressively responsible experience in a flying component of the US military establishment in assignments that would normally qualify for progression to the position of Wing Commander or its equivalent. Assignments should have been of kinds that enabled the applicant to have gained and demonstrated a knowledge of tactical or strategic warfare, including techniques of employment or appropriate type of aircraft, military administration, personnel management and logistics. At least one year of the specialized experience must have been of a level of difficulty and responsibility comparable to that of the GS-14 grade in the Federal service. SUBSTITUTION: - Completion of Air Force pilot or navigator training or equivalent training in other US military establishments for heavier-than-air aircraft may be substituted for one year of general experience. - Satisfactory completion of Air War College, Air Command and Staff College, or equivalent in another of the US military establishments, may be substituted for one year of specialized experience. - Each year of service in a Reserve component of the US military establishment in assignments that normally would result in progression into the position of Wing Commander, and in which the flying requirements specialized by Air Force regulation have been met, may be credited for three months of general or specialized experience. The substitution, may not be made for periods of Reserve service which occurred concurrently with periods of fulltime experience for which credit is assigned CERTIFICATION: Must have been awarded or qualify for a USAF Command Pilot or USAF Command Navigator or USAF Master Combat Systems Officer (CSO) or Command RPA Pilot or Master Air Battle Manager rating or 15 years of total rated service and hold a valid aviation service aeronautical order. MINIMUM INSTRUMENT HOURS REQUIRED: Must hold a valid USAF instrument rating or other equivalent military or civilian rating. MINIMUM FLYING HOURS: Applicants must have logged a minimum of 2,500 Total Military Flight Time and previous instructor qualification is required in any MDS and have actively flown within the past 8 years. Federal Time-In-Grade (TIG) Requirement for General Schedule (GS) Positions: Applicants must have served at least 52 weeks at the GS- 14 grade level or higher grade (or equivalent in an alternate pay system) within the Federal Civil Service to be considered for referral. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of planning, organizing, coordinating, directing, and controlling activities, operations, and resources of a flying organization; and mentoring, motivating, and appraising a staff through subordinate supervisors. 2. Knowledge of the operations of a wing, various Air Force Reserve entities, other MAJCOMs and Air Force, and their relationships in overall management and execution of military operations, evaluations, and missions. 3. Knowledge of public relations and human relations as applicable to managing an organization. 4. Knowledge of rated aviator expertise and skill in its application, as either a pilot or navigator. 5. Knowledge of tactical and strategic warfare, and wartime readiness posture; Skill in exercising tact and diplomacy in dealing various individuals when accomplishing duties. 6. Skill in effective oral and written communication and public speaking to manage the operations of the assigned wing, communicate issues to subordinates, other officials, and the public, and to advocate the Air Force Reserve. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MajorDuties: The primary purpose of this position is to serve as Air Reserve Technician (ART) officer to serve as the senior ART/Commander and as such, be responsible for planning, organizing, coordinating, directing, and controlling the fulltime activities and operations of the wing. As Commander of a Numbered Air Force (NAF), or Wing which is either a host organization or an organization tenanted on an Air Force installation of another command, plans, organizes, directs and controls the activities and operations of the unit through subordinate functional chief positions. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: The Installation Management Command Directorate-Europe (ID-E), Executive Officer serves as the primary administrative lead and technical expert supporting the Command Group. Operating with high discretion, the incumbent manages critical logistical, personnel, and document control workflows. Acting as a strategic bridge, they translate higher headquarters directives into actionable plans and coordinate responses across subordinate units to ensure seamless mission integration.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. Wiesbaden is without a doubt one of the most attractive cities in Germany. The capital city of Hessen is sometimes referred to as "Nice of the North" and rightfully so considering the many mansions, the historic Kurhaus, the casino and the State Theater. Wiesbaden is well known as a great spa city since ancient times. It has 27 hot, saline springs and its mild climate and park-like setting continue to make it a popular resort and conference center. Wiesbaden has an abundance of leisure activities, providing a cosmopolitan atmosphere blended with an attractive cultural ambiance, extraordinary architecture and marked by endearing charm. Located in a premier wine growing area on the Rhine River only 20 minutes from the Frankfurt International Airport. Efficient mass transportation systems are readily available. Visit the Wiesbaden Army Community website at: www.wiesbaden.army.mil for local garrison support and http://www.wiesbaden.de for city plans and attractions.
MajorDuties: Serves as the key advisor to the Command Group for administration and coordination of operations, acting on behalf of senior leadership to task staff and subordinate commanders.
Manages and coordinates diverse operational activities, integrating program elements to ensure mission accomplishment and formulating supporting policies, plans, and objectives.
Supports mission and force structure development by creating and maintaining IMCOM-E Strategic Initiatives, ensuring Command priorities are nested within Army and IMCOM strategy.
Performs planning and implementation by analyzing mission assignments, establishing program objectives, and developing current and long-range plans for the organization.
Provides a thorough review of all flag officer correspondence prior to signature, ensuring coordination, legal sufficiency, and alignment with Command policies and programs.
Serves as a first-line supervisor to front office staff, planning work, setting priorities, evaluating performance, and managing administrative and personnel matters.

If selected at the GS-09 level, you may be non-competitively promoted to the full performance level of GS-11 when eligible and at management's discretion. In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. For the GS-09 Level: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Performing administrative and technical support duties for major projects; 2) Utilizing software and maintaining electronic databases; AND 3) Preparing reports and briefings to disseminate information on project execution. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-07). OR Education: Master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Program/Project Management. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the first year (total graduate semester hours minus 18) by 18. Add the two percentages. For the GS-11 level: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes: 1) Applying financial management, contracting, and scheduling principles to provide support for construction projects; 2) Utilizing databases, spreadsheets, and project management software programs; 3) Conducting qualitative and quantitative analysis to evaluate program effectiveness; AND 4) Providing superior customer service to construction project stakeholders. This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the second lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-09). OR Education: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, such as: Program/Project Management. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. To compute the percentage of the requirements, divide your total months of experience by 12. Then divide the total number of completed graduate semester hours (or equivalent) beyond the second year (total graduate semester hours minus 36) by 18. Add the two percentages. Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-07 or GS-09).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position provides support and assistance to Project Managers (PMs) who oversee projects from inception through construction completion.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Build Strong With Us at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), where engineering excellence meets public service. As the Nation's premier engineering, design, and construction management agency, we deliver innovative and efficient solutions that strengthen national security, support economic growth, and reduce disaster risks for communities across the country. At USACE, you will find meaningful work, collaborative teams, and opportunities to grow your career while making a lasting impact. We seek talented professionals with vision, creativity, leadership, and technical expertise to help solve some of the Nation's toughest engineering challenges. Build your purpose. Build your profession. Build your future. Discover why USACE is a great place to work and Build Strong With Us.
MajorDuties: Under the direction of the project manager (PM), plan and schedule tasks and monitor the progress of project completion. Projects vary in type and involve MILCON and Operation and Maintenance projects throughout the project life cycle.

Collect project execution data from PMs. Enter and maintain data into electronic databases. Prepare a variety of reports for upward reporting, project status reviews with customers, and other data calls as required.
Support the planning and execution of Architect/Engineer (A/E) contracts for construction projects.

Assist the PM in planning and evaluating all phases of project control. Coordinate with the PM, the Project Delivery Team, and District Supervisors to disseminate information about the project schedule and any project issues needing resolution.

Perform a variety of administrative and technical support duties, including maintaining and distributing documents and files to other sections and branches as assigned, and preparing graphs, charts and other materials for briefings and meetings.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-03, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-13 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience includes planning, organizing, and directing Center-level human resources, civilian, military, and manpower functions through subordinate supervisors. Experience also includes advising senior leadership and coordinating with headquarters to develop and implement integrated human resources policies. Experience in applying management principles to analyze operations, restructure organizations, optimize resources, and execute supervisory duties such as mentoring staff and recommending candidates. Experience also includes communicating strategic positions and building effective working relationships with senior leaders, General Officers, and Senior Executive Service members across installations. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Mastery of advanced management and organizational principles and practices along with a comprehensive knowledge of human resources functions, e.g., civilian personnel, military personnel, manpower, etc., to develop and implement integrated approaches and solutions to significant human resources concerns and issues. Knowledge of USAF, AFMC, and AFLCMC organizations, programs, missions, and functions to analyze and determine human resources plans, programs, and initiatives to support customers' current and future requirements. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the functions and mentor, motivate, and appraise the staff of the directorate through subordinate supervisors. Ability to analyze, plan, and adjust work operations of one or more organizational segments to meet program requirements and objectives within available resources. Ability to communicate, both orally and in writing, to achieve stated positions or to make an adequate case for a particular strategy which may or may not be readily accepted but is the best solution to achieve overall AFLCMC goals. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

The primary purpose of this position is to deliver center-level human resources policy, planning, resourcing, and services that enhances the Center's ability to support the warfighter as the Director of AFLCMC/DP.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. Click here to view the AF Civilian Employment Eligibility Guide: US Citizen This job announcement may close at any time - apply now!
MajorDuties: Exercises supervisory personnel management responsibilities at least 25% of the time. Directs, coordinates, and oversees work through subordinate supervisors. Plans, organizes, and directs the Center-level activities for the Directorate, Personnel Division. Provides subordinate supervisors and staff with direction and advice regarding policies, procedures, and guidelines. Reviews and structures organization to optimize use of resources and maximize efficiency and effectiveness of the organization. Serves as a confidential advisor to the Center Commander, Vice-Commander, and Executive Director for matters related to human resources. Works directly with manpower, military personnel, and civilian personnel offices at HQ Air Force Material Command (AFMC) and HQ USAF levels to develop and implement human resources policies across the Center. Represents the Personnel Directorate with a variety of installation and functional area organizations. Establishes, develops, and maintains effective working relationships with all levels of management and human resources personnel, including General Officers and Senior Executive Service members, located at Wright Patterson AFB, other AFMC Centers, HQ AFMC, and Air Force. Advises staff regarding policies, procedures, and directives of higher level management or headquarters. With the director, selects or recommends candidates for subordinate positions, taking into consideration skills and qualifications, mission requirements, and EEO and diversity objectives.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: ACQUISITION PROGRAM MANAGEMENT SPECIALIST - DIRECT HIRE AUTHORITY
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-03, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-13 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in serving as a technical and acquisition advisor to senior MAJCOM, Air Force, and DoD leadership regarding broad Special Access Program (SAP) operations, utilizing a mastery-level knowledge of the complete materiel acquisition life-cycle from requirements generation through test execution. Experience also includes applying acquisition procedures, strategic planning, and the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process to advance capabilities, execute funds, and manage risk across all major program areas. Experience in analyzing, planning, and adjusting the work operations of subordinate organizational segments to meet program objectives within available resources and strict safety and security regulations for classified areas. Experience also includes establishing effective working relationships across DoD agencies to negotiate, defend, and clearly communicate highly complex technical and acquisition concepts to senior leaders, decision-makers, and non-specialists at various security levels. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: Combinations of successfully completed post-high school education and experience may be used to meet total qualification requirements. NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts. IDEAL CANDIDATE: Position serves as a senior acquisition and technical advisor to the AFMC Special Access Program Management Office (SAPMO) and as the recognized Special Access Program/Special Access Required (SAP/SAR) developmental planning, capability requirements, and Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) Program Objective Memorandum (POM) expert. Position spans the entire breadth of MAJCOM's SAP portfolio and related missions and recognized as the MAJCOM authority on cross capability and functional SAP activities. Ideal Candidate will provide senior level Program Management insight, expert guidance and advice regarding cost, schedule and performance of SAP/SAR programs to Center/MAJCOM leadership, Air Force Headquarters Staff, and/or other services/agencies. Based on unique work environment and special program requirements and processes, position requires Special Access Program/Special Access Required (SAP/SAR) experience. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Mastery level knowledge of the effective use and application of acquisition procedures, elements, and techniques to advance capabilities and improve materiel resource planning, execution, and assessment across all major AFMC special program areas. Knowledge of the policies, principles, concepts, guidance, procedures, techniques, and methodologies pertaining to acquisition capability development and strategic planning and programming. Specifically, knowledge of current acquisition Program Management principles such as requirements generation, funds execution, contracting methodologies, milestone approvals, risk assessments, systems engineering management, and test execution to cover the entire materiel acquisition life-cycle. Knowledge of the mission, roles, function, organizational structures, and operation of DoD and Air Force organizations to provide command level staff guidance. Ability to analyze, plan, and adjust work operations of subordinate organizational segments to meet program requirements and objectives within technical capabilities and available resources. Ability to communicate orally and in writing, clearly, concisely with technical accuracy to senior leaders at various security levels. In-depth knowledge of the acquisition process from developmental planning to the end of program lifecycles to support the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPB) process. This knowledge should be current and run the gamut from program office to center-level process through Air Staff and OSD process. A high degree of analytical ability to discern changes to program security levels, acquisition phases, and funding across AFMC centers and AF groups. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures to include classified areas. Ability to analyze, plan and adjust work operations of one of more organizational segments to meet program requirements and objectives within available resources. Communication skills and abilities, verbal and nonverbal, in conjunction with the ability to present and influence decisions by the high levels of management, both within and outside of the directorate, and to support and defend recommendations to those levels. Skill to negotiate and/or defend findings and program support concepts and skill in preparing and presenting highly complex technical material or highly complex issues, or both, to non-specialists. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: SUPERVISORY MANAGEMENT ANALYST - DIRECT HIRE AUTHORITY
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in planning, organizing, and directing the operations of a Manpower Office, which includes exercising supervisory personnel management responsibilities to assign work, set organizational priorities, and evaluate performance. Expertise extends to applying advanced qualitative and quantitative methods, management engineering principles, and analytical techniques to conduct comprehensive studies on manpower requirements, organizational structure, workload, and program cost. Experience in advising commanders, directors, and senior staff on complex manpower and organization matters, including organizational realignment, mission changes, and resource assessment. Background includes communicating effectively both orally and in writing to deliver briefings, coordinate actions with high-level stakeholders, and resolve critical issues affecting program efficiency and organizational performance. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of manpower and organization principles, methods, processes, and analytical techniques used to assess manpower requirements, organizational structure, workload, and resources use. Knowledge of qualitative and quantitative methods used to apply management engineering principles, management analysis concepts, work measurement, program cost analysis, and resource assessment. Knowledge of the missions, functions, programs, and organizational relationships of serviced activities sufficient to conduct studies, assess manning and skill-level needs, and recommend supportable manpower and organization actions. Knowledge of manpower resource principles and techniques as they relate to organizational realignment, mission change, closure actions, outsourcing, privatization, insourcing, and related manpower studies when applicable. Knowledge of safety and security requirements, practices, and procedures applicable to the work environment. Skill in applying analytical and evaluative techniques to identify, assess, and resolve issues affecting program efficiency, effectiveness, cost, workload, manpower requirements, and organizational performance. Skill in planning, organizing, and directing comprehensive manpower and organization analyses involving diverse organizations, functions, missions, and work processes. Skill in advising commanders, directors, supervisors, and staff on manpower and organization matters and developing recommendations that are clear, supportable, and mission-focused. Ability to plan, organize, and direct the work of a small to medium-sized organization, including assigning work, setting priorities, evaluating performance, developing employees, and improving work processes. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, to prepare reports, present briefings, explain complex manpower issues, and coordinate actions with customers and stakeholders. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Clerical and Administrative Support. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in planning, coordinating, and executing military protocol activities and distinguished visits for senior executive leadership ("Top Five"), including changes of command, promotions, retirements, and executive-level conferences. This includes researching visitor backgrounds and applying comprehensive knowledge of DAF, AFMC, and civilian protocol courtesies, ranks, and precedence to prevent breaches of custom. Experience also includes managing event budgets to project and document expenditures, developing integrated execution plans under tight deadlines, and communicating persuasively both verbally and in writing to diverse internal and external stakeholders to achieve mission goals. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Comprehensive knowledge of WPAFB and its tenant organizational structure, functions, policies, and operations, etc., to ensure programs planned for visitors to WPAFB are accurate, comprehensive, informative, and are conducted within acceptable parameters in accordance with 88th ABW and AFMC policies. Comprehensive knowledge of organizational components, including the function/location/organizational structure and activities of other AFMC units, major commands, DAF, tri-service's executive and legislative liaison offices to determine types of programs appropriate for presentation to visitors from those organizations and the level of protocol courtesies to be accorded them based on rank, precedence, and significance to the mission. Comprehensive knowledge of proper civilian and military protocol courtesies to be accorded to visitors from both the United States and foreign governments that contributes to the ability to research special protocols and visiting requirements of foreign and U.S. dignitaries (etiquette manuals and guides, DAF/AFMC policies, regulations and procedures). Working knowledge of pertinent budgeting and accounting practices to project, monitor and document collections and expenditures. Ability to communicate both verbally and in writing, to achieve stated positions, or to make an adequate case for a particular strategy which may or may not be readily accepted but is the best solution to achieve overall mission goals. Ability to develop, analyze, evaluate and integrate plans and other documents related to assigned functions. Able to plan individual workload to meet deadlines. IDEAL CANDIDATE: We are seeking a candidate with a strong Protocol background: either 12+ months at the MAJCOM level or 24+ months at the Wing/NAF level. Furthermore, successful completion of the USAF Protocol Fundamentals Course and other recognized Protocol professional development curricula is highly desirable. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MajorDuties: Assist with implementing policies and procedures for Protocol. Plans, formulates, manages, advises, coordinates, directs, administers and executes protocol activities including: changes of command, conferences, executive level meetings, retirements, promotions, commander's call, visits by distinguished official guests and groups, special presentations and awards programs, special ceremonies, special purpose conferences and projects in support of the AFMC Commander, Command Chief, Deputy Commander, Executive Director and Director of Staff ("Top Five"). Working knowledge of pertinent budgeting and accounting practices to project, monitor and document expenditures.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-02, equivalent to the next lower grade GS-11 or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is experience in directing and executing operations planning, readiness, and scheduling activities in support of Air Force Force Generation (AFFORGEN) and contingency operations. This includes advising on crisis action planning while utilizing the Joint Crisis Action Process (JCAP), Global Command and Control System (GCCS), and Joint Operation Planning and Execution System (JOPES). Experience also includes serving as the expert for the Deliberate and Crisis Action Planning and Execution Segments (DCAPES) program, providing Global Force Management (GFM) decision support, and coordinating requirements across the Joint Staff, Air Staff, and combatant commands. Additionally, experience in supporting Functional Area Managers (FAMs) on deployment processes, implementing safety regulations, driving process improvements, and delivering clear, strategic briefings to senior leadership.. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. OR COMBINING EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: Combinations of successfully completed post-high school education and experience may be used to meet total qualification requirements KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge and understanding and working knowledge of the Joint Crisis Action Process (JCAP), Global Command and Control System (GCCS), and GCCS AF. Experience with and understanding of the Joint Operation Planning an Execution System (JOPES) and expert knowledge with and understanding of the AF Deliberate and Crisis Action Planning and Execution Segments (DCAPES). Knowledge of the structure and relationships that exist between the Joint Staff, the Air Staff, the combatant commanders, the component commanders, the AEF Center, the AF MAJCOMs and AF bases in conducting Joint and AF planning. Ability to develop instructional products and deliver briefings and training in an effective manner. Knowledge of AF organizational structure and the role of deliberate and crisis planning within each. Understanding of AFMCs unique relationship within the standard AF MAJCOM/base structure to include, understanding the dual roles of AFMC bases as AF bases and also product, tests and logistics centers. Knowledge of safety and security regulations, practices, and procedures. Skill in understanding and working knowledge of the AF Force Generation concept and principles, to include understanding the AFMC role in the planning and execution of deployment operations. Working knowledge and understanding of the role and activities of the AF functional area managers (FAMs) to include expertise in operational processes necessary for FAMs to execute their duties. Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing. Working knowledge of processes identification and documentation, including process improvement. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-09, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes: (1) Working with administrative analysis and problem-solving techniques to evaluate staff processes, interpret administrative data, and develop recommendations to improve the efficiency of executive support operations; (2) Working with administrative structures, staff roles, and command channels of the Organization and higher-echelon Air Force/DoD organizations to effectively coordinate executive taskings and provide administrative advisory services; and (3) Working with advanced executive support systems and software (e.g., MS Office Suite, SharePoint, Defense Travel System) to manage complex scheduling, coordinate executive travel, generate data-driven reports, and facilitate high-visibility logistics. OR EDUCATION: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. degree or LL.M which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position, if related. NOTE: You must submit a copy of your transcripts. OR Combination of Education and Experience: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-09 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-11 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Knowledge of administrative analysis and problem-solving techniques to evaluate staff processes, interpret administrative data, and develop recommendations to improve the efficiency of Wing executive support operations. Knowledge of the administrative structures, staff roles, and command channels of the Wing and higher-echelon Air Force/DoD organizations to effectively coordinate executive taskings and provide administrative advisory services. Knowledge of administrative rules and skill in using executive support systems (e.g., MS Office, SharePoint, DTS) to manage complex scheduling, executive travel, and high-visibility logistics. Skill in written and verbal communication to prepare clear, concise, and accurate reports, briefings, and correspondence for senior leaders and external stakeholders. Skill in planning and managing short and long-term projects and initiatives, including the ability to identify resources, track milestones, and resolve program shortfalls. Ability to exercise independent judgment and use tact and diplomacy to build successful cross-functional teams and resolve complex problems impacting the command mission. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Benefits of joining U.S. Army Garrison Yuma, Yuma, AZ, include ride share opportunities; on-post surplus housing; and access to Morale, Welfare & Recreation services like child-care and youth activities for school-aged children, food and beverage facilities, fitness center, pool, and discount military theme park tickets. For those living on-post there is an on-post elementary school for grades kindergarten thru 5th grade. Benefits of being an Army Professional include unique training and professional development opportunities, DoD and Federal Leadership Development programs, paid federal holidays, sick leave and annual leave accrued per pay period based on time in service, retirement benefits, 401K matching contributions, work life enrichment such Employee Assistance Programs, and the Army Civilian Fitness and Health Promotion Program. YPG is located near the Arizona-California-Mexico border, approximately 15 miles north of the outskirts of the city of Yuma (pop 87,000), Arizona. Yuma is a 2.5-hour drive from San Diego, CA and Phoenix, AZ, along Interstate Highway 8, and a 5-6 hour drive from Las Vegas, NV, in the heart of the great Sonoran desert where the US Army tests medium and long range artillery, aircraft target acquisition equipment and armament, armored and wheeled vehicles, and a variety of munitions, and personnel and supply parachute systems to ensure that America's ground forces have the equipment necessary to win our nation's battles.
MajorDuties: Assists in the development and implementation of effective marketing plans that support organizational goals, increase customer awareness, and drive program participation.
Contributes to comprehensive publicity, promotional, sales, and merchandising strategies tailored to target audiences and local market conditions.
Helps coordinate integrated marketing campaigns across print, digital, broadcast, and on-site channels to ensure consistent messaging and branding.
Provides recommendations on media layouts, advertising copy, photography, graphic design, print materials, and broadcast releases to improve campaign effectiveness.
Reviews marketing results and customer feedback to identify opportunities for improvement and support future planning efforts.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Details.Benefits: Working for Army Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF) can offer numerous advantages. Army NAF employment can provide a sense of pride and fulfillment, as you'll be supporting communities comprised of military and civilian personnel, and their families, which contributes to the Department of Defense's overall mission. We offer a wide range of career opportunities, including jobs in childcare, recreation, hospitality, and more.
